Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3, PDF p.21

5.3 Arrangement of information

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1, PDF p.21

5.3.1.1 General Requirements

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.1, PDF p.21

5.3.1.1.1 The presentation of objects, text messages and buttons shall be possible on several levels. Within those levels, they shall be allocated to areas of the ERTMS/ETCS DMI.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.2, PDF p.21

5.3.1.1.2 Objects, text messages and buttons presented within the same level shall form a ‘window’. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 21 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.3, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.3 The default windows of the ERTMS/ETCS DMI shall be the total image display area with the allocation of objects, text messages and buttons as described in chapters 8 and 9.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.4, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.4 A default window shall not cover any other window.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.5, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.5 While a sub-level window is activated, it shall cover the parent level window. A window shall be covered partially or totally by the sub-level window depending on the size of the sub-level window. The latest sub-level window shall be active meaning that all other windows shall not respond to any driver input.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.6, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.6 A window shall be composed of: a) a unique window title giving the topic of the window (e.g. Train data); b) one or several areas for the content of the window e.g. input fields, buttons,..; c) a [Close] button closing the window and returning to the parent window; d) possibly, a [Next] button: to be used to select the next window related to the same topic; e) possibly, a [Previous] button: to be used to select the previous window related to the same topic.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.7, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.7 Exception: On a default window, 5.3.1.1.6 shall not apply.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.8, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.8 Exception: When using a soft key technology, if there are several windows related to the same topic (e.g. Train data), the [Close] button shall be replaced by the [Previous] button on the windows following the first one. (see chapter 10.3.6).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.8.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.8.1, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.8.1 Note: When using a soft key technology, for this kind of windows, there are not enough keys to present all necessary navigation buttons. Consequently, the driver will have to go back to the first window of the topic to find the [Close] button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.9

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.9, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.9 The scrolling between various windows related to the same topic shall not be circular i.e. the first window shall not scroll to the last one and vice-versa.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.1.10

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.1.10, PDF p.22

5.3.1.1.10 Note: For more details about the navigation buttons, see chapter 5.3.2.7.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.1.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.1.2.1, PDF p.22

5.3.1.2.1 A window title area shall meet the following requirements: a) the height shall be 24 cells; b) the background colour shall be black; c) it shall contain a text label identifying the window; d) the text label on the window title area shall be grey; e) it shall be positioned at the top of the window; f) it shall cover the width of the window, unless stated otherwise for specific windows; g) if the number of DMI objects (e.g. buttons, text messages, input data fields) related to the topic of a window cannot fit on the window area(s), the text label on the window title shall include between brackets the sequence number of the current Version 3.6.0 PAGE 22 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface window and the total number of windows related to the same topic separated by a slash e.g. (1/2).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.1.1, PDF p.23

5.3.2.1.1 When using a touch screen technology, the size of the touch sensitive surface of the button shall be equal to the size of the visible surface of the button, unless stated otherwise for specific buttons.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.2, PDF p.23

5.3.2.2 Button operation feedback

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.2.1, PDF p.23

5.3.2.2.1 Activation of a button shall be accompanied by feedback: a) visual, and b) tactile and/or audible.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.3.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.3.1, PDF p.23

5.3.2.3.1 The buttons shall be labelled with a language dependent text or with a symbol (see chapter 13).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.3.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.3.2, PDF p.23

5.3.2.3.2 The text label or the symbol shall be centred on the button, unless stated otherwise for specific buttons.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.4.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.4.1, PDF p.23

5.3.2.4.1 The background colour of a button shall be the Dark Blue (background) colour, unless stated otherwise for specific buttons.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.5.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.5.1, PDF p.23

5.3.2.5.1 A button may have three different states: “enabled”, “disabled” and “pressed”.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.5.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.5.2, PDF p.23

5.3.2.5.2 An “enabled” button shall be shown slightly lifted from the background by displaying a border (see 5.1.1.1.3).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.5.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.5.3, PDF p.23

5.3.2.5.3 A “pressed” button shall be shown slightly into the background by not displaying its border.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.5.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.5.4, PDF p.23

5.3.2.5.4 Only one button shall be in the “pressed” state at the same time.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.5.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.5.5, PDF p.23

5.3.2.5.5 A “disabled” button shall be: a) shown as an “enabled” button with the text label in dark grey or with a specific symbol, or b) not shown at all.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.5.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.5.6, PDF p.23

5.3.2.5.6 Note: For soft key technology, the border of the button refers to the border around its label part.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6, PDF p.23

5.3.2.6 Button types Version 3.6.0 PAGE 23 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6.1, PDF p.24

5.3.2.6.1 There are three ways in which an “enabled” button can react to driver selections (up, down or delay).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6.2, PDF p.24

5.3.2.6.2 On selection by the driver, the up-type button (see Figure 3) shall change to the “pressed” state and the ‘click’ sound shall be played. As long as the button remains pressed by the driver, the button shall remain in the “pressed” state. After releasing the selection, the button state shall exit the “pressed” state and a valid button activation shall be considered by the onboard (implying that the function associated to the button is initiated).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6.3, PDF p.24

5.3.2.6.3 If, when using touch screen technology, the driver selection continues, but outside the up-type button itself (the finger slides out of the sensitive area of the button) the button shall return to the ”enabled” state and no valid button activation shall be considered by the onboard. When the driver selection moves back to the button (the finger slides back onto the sensitive area of the button) the button shall be shown in the “pressed” state again, but this time without the ‘click’ sound played. button state button activation taken into account enabled pressed time driver action on button not not pressed pressed pressed time Figure 3 - Activation of an up-type button

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6.4, PDF p.24

5.3.2.6.4 On selection by the driver, the down-type button (see Figure 4) shall alter from ”enabled” to “pressed” and immediately back to the ”enabled” state. The ‘click’ sound shall be played and a valid button activation shall be considered by the onboard.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6.5, PDF p.24

5.3.2.6.5 A down-type button can have a repeat function if the button remains pressed by the driver for longer than 1.5 seconds. After 1.5 seconds, the repeat function shall consider valid button activations each 0.3 sec; the visual and audible indications are as if the driver was pressing on the button every 0.3 sec. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 24 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface button activation button = taken into account state

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 1.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 1.5, PDF p.25

1.5 s enabled pressed time driver repeat function action (if needed) on

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 1.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 1.5, PDF p.25

1.5 s button not not pressed pressed pressed Figure 4 - Activation of a down-type button

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6.6, PDF p.25

5.3.2.6.6 The delay-type button is similar to the up-type button but with a delay (see Figure 5). On selection by the driver, the delay-type button shall change to the “pressed” state and the ‘click’ sound shall be played. The button shall then toggle every 0.25 seconds between the “pressed” and “enabled” states as long as the button remains pressed by the driver. After 2 seconds, if the button is still pressed by the driver, the button shall change again to the “pressed” state and the procedure according to the up-type button shall be followed. If the button is pressed by the driver for less than the 2 seconds, the button shall return to the ”enabled” state, the procedure with the 2 seconds timer shall be reset and no valid button activation shall be considered by the onboard

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.6.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.6.7, PDF p.25

5.3.2.6.7 If, when using touch screen technology, the driver selection continues, but outside the delay-type button itself (the finger slides out of the sensitive area of the button) the button shall return to the ”enabled” state, the procedure with the 2 seconds timer shall be reset and no valid button activation shall be considered by the onboard. When the driver selection moves back to the delay-type button (the finger slides back onto the sensitive area of the button), the procedure with the 2 seconds timer shall start again but this time without the ‘click’ sound played. button state enabled time Version 3.6.0 PAGE 25 OF 263 desserp button activation = taken into account 2 s driver action on 2 s button not not pressed pressed pressed delbane pressed desserp delbane desserp delbane desserp delbane ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface Figure 5 - Activation of a delay-type button

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7 Navigation buttons

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7.1, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7.1 The following navigation buttons shall be used where appropriate: a) [Close] button: to be used for closing a window and returning to the parent window; symbols NA11 of chapter 13 shall be used. b) [Enter] button: to be used to accept the input field data value; the [Enter] button finishes the handling of the current selection; symbol NA20 of chapter 13 shall be used (soft key technology). c) [Next] button: to be used to select the next window related to the same topic using the symbol NA17. d) [Previous] button: to be used to select the previous window related to the same topic using the symbols NA18. e) [Delete] button: to be used to delete the just entered character, symbol NA21 of chapter 13 shall be used. f) [Up] or [Down] button: to be used to scroll respectively up and down in lists; symbols NA13 and NA14 of chapter 13 shall be used. g) [Scale Up] or [Scale Down] button: to be used respectively to shorten/enlarge a distance scale; symbols NA03, NA04 (touch screen technology) and NA07, NA08 (soft key technology) of chapter 13 shall be used. h) Intentionally deleted. i) [More] button: to be used to present the next predefined choices of a dedicated keyboard, symbol NA23 of chapter 13 shall be used.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7.2, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7.2 The [Delete], [Up] and [Down] buttons shall be down-type buttons with a repeat function.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7.3, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7.3 The [Enter] button shall be an up-type unless an operational data check rule is not satisfied in which case it becomes a delay-type button (see 10.3.4 for further details).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7.4, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7.4 The [Next], [Previous], [Scale Up], [Scale Down] and [More] navigation buttons shall always be up-type buttons.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7.5, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7.5 For the [Up], [Down], [Scale Up], [Scale Down], [Next] and [Previous] buttons, they shall be disabled if their respective function does not lead to any change in the display.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7.6, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7.6 In some situations, the [Close] button (see 11.7) and the [Enter] button (see 10.3.4) shall also be disabled.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.3.2.7.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.3.2.7.7, PDF p.26

5.3.2.7.7 If the buttons in “disabled” state are shown (see 5.3.2.5.5), the symbols NA05, NA06, NA09, NA10, NA12, NA15, NA16, NA18.2, NA19 and NA22 shall respectively replace the symbols NA03, NA04, NA07, NA08, NA11, NA13, NA14, NA17, NA18 and NA20.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4, PDF p.26

5.4 Acknowledgements Version 3.6.0 PAGE 26 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.1, PDF p.27

5.4.1.1 When using touch screen technology, when a driver’s acknowledgement is required and can be displayed, the ERTMS/ETCS DMI shall always offer an acknowledgement (Ack) located on the total image display area itself. In addition, it may offer the following possibility for the acknowledgement (Ack): a button positioned in an ergonomic location on the driver’s desk.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.1.1, PDF p.27

5.4.1.1.1 Note: The location of the acknowledgement button onto the total image display area varies depending on the object to be acknowledged. See chapter 8 for the specific area(s) becoming the acknowledgement button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.1.2, PDF p.27

5.4.1.1.2 Note: Depending on the situation, it may happen that a driver’s acknowledgement is required but cannot be displayed yet; see 5.4.1.9 and 5.4.1.11.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.2, PDF p.27

5.4.1.2 When using soft key technology, when a driver’s acknowledgement is required and can be displayed, the ERTMS/ETCS DMI shall always offer an acknowledgement (Ack) via the soft key H7 showing the symbol DR04. In addition, it may offer the following possibility for the acknowledgement (Ack): a button positioned on an ergonomic location on the driver’s desk.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.3, PDF p.27

5.4.1.3 Unless stated otherwise, the Ack-button shall be an up-type button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.4, PDF p.27

5.4.1.4 When using touch screen technology, the area displaying the related object or text message shall become the Ack-button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.5, PDF p.27

5.4.1.5 When a driver’s acknowledgement is displayed, a yellow flashing frame shall be used to surround the related object or text message and sound Sinfo (see chapter 14) shall be played.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.6, PDF p.27

5.4.1.6 When using soft key technology, an additional frame around H7 (i.e. the ‘Ack’ label) shall also flash.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.6.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.6.1, PDF p.27

5.4.1.6.1 Note: in the soft key technology, 2 flashing frames are displayed.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.7, PDF p.27

5.4.1.7 Only one request for Acknowledgement (Ack) at any given time shall be presented to the driver.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.8, PDF p.27

5.4.1.8 As soon as the current object or text message has been acknowledged, the Ack-button and the yellow flashing frame(s) related to this object or text message shall disappear.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.9

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.9, PDF p.27

5.4.1.9 If there is more than one object or text message for which a driver’s acknowledgement is required, they shall be managed according to a FIFO principle with a delay of 1 sec between their display i.e. the next object or text message and its related request of Acknowledgement shall be displayed 1 second after the current object or text message has been acknowledged.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.10

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.10, PDF p.27

5.4.1.10 The ERTMS/ETCS DMI shall display text messages that do not have to be acknowledged only when the FIFO list does not contain any text message(s) which has to be acknowledged (see 8.2.3.4 for details about display of text messages).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.4.1.11

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.4.1.11, PDF p.27

5.4.1.11 If a driver’s acknowledgement is required when a data entry window is displayed, see

5.5.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS DMI shall be able to display text in all languages pre-configured onboard.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 5.5.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 5.5.1.2, PDF p.28

5.5.1.2 In addition to the settings menu allowing access to the language window (see chapter 11.2.4), the ERTMS/ETCS DMI may offer the following possibility to access it: a button positioned on an ergonomic location on the driver’s desk.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 6.2.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 6.2.1.1, PDF p.31

6.2.1.1 In order to position areas, objects and buttons onto the total grid array, a cartesian coordinate system shall be used with the direction of the horizontal axis (X) from left to right and with the direction of the vertical axis (Y) from top to bottom.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 6.2.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 6.2.1.2, PDF p.31

6.2.1.2 Unless stated otherwise, the origin of the coordinate system shall be the top left corner of the area or of the group of areas containing the (sub)area, the object or the button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 6.2.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 6.2.1.3, PDF p.31

6.2.1.3 Unless stated otherwise, the position of an area, an object or a button shall be given by the coordinates (X,Y) of its top left corner.

8.2.3.2 Level information

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.1, PDF p.78

8.2.3.2.1 Level information consists of three elements: a) the current ERTMS/ETCS level; b) an ERTMS/ETCS level announcement with acknowledgement; c) an ERTMS/ETCS level announcement.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.2, PDF p.78

8.2.3.2.2 When the current ERTMS/ETCS level is valid and equal to 0, NTC (except in the modes SN and NL), 1, 2 or 3, it shall be displayed in area C8 (see Figure 57).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.2.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.3, PDF p.78

8.2.3.2.3 If the current ERTMS/ETCS level is unknown or invalid, no DMI object shall be displayed in area C8. Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.6, PDF p.79

8.2.3.2.6 No ERTMS/ETCS level announcement shall be displayed as long as a mode acknowledgement is displayed in C1.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.7, PDF p.79

8.2.3.2.7 If no acknowledgement is required for the ERTMS/ETCS level announcement, the symbol LE06, LE08, LE10, LE12 or LE14 (see chapter 13) shall be used, depending on the ERTMS/ETCS level announcement.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.2.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.8, PDF p.79

8.2.3.2.8 If an acknowledgement is required for the ERTMS/ETCS level announcement, the symbol LE07, LE09, LE11, LE13, LE15 (see chapter 13) shall be used, depending on the next ERTMS/ETCS level announcement. For these symbols, the requirements specified in 5.4 shall apply. As long as the train has not yet reached the trackside location from where the acknowledgement is required or as soon as the ERTMS/ETCS level announcement is acknowledged, the symbol LE06, LE08, LE10, LE12 or LE14 (see chapter 13) shall replace respectively LE07, LE09, LE11, LE13, LE15.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.2.9

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.9, PDF p.79

8.2.3.2.9 For level NTC, the distinct abbreviation of the corresponding National System (its definition is inherent to the National System and is outside the scope of this specification) shall be displayed instead of the text “NTC” as shown in symbol LE02, LE08, LE09.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.2.10

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.2.10, PDF p.79

8.2.3.2.10 The space used for characters of the National System abbreviation shall not exceed an area of 48 x 19 (w x h) cells in the C8 and shall comply with the minimum size of characters as defined in 5.1.2. ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.4.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.4.6, PDF p.85

8.2.3.4.6 The following applies to all text messages: a) The text messages shall be presented in white colour. b) The local time of appearance shall be attached to the first line of a displayed text message. It shall be separated from the first character of the displayed text by an indent of 10 cells. This local time shall be in the format ‘hh:mm’ with a 24 hours time reference. c) If a text message does not fit in one area, it shall continue inside the next area (i.e. the text message will be composed of several lines). The next lines shall be aligned with the first character of the displayed text (see Figure 62).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.4.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.4.7, PDF p.85

8.2.3.4.7 The following applies to text messages that do not have to be acknowledged: a) The text messages shall be divided into two groups. The first group shall contain the system status messages and the important plain/fixed text messages received from trackside. The second group shall contain the auxiliary plain/fixed text messages received from trackside. b) The text messages of the first group shall be displayed above the text messages of the second group. c) The text messages of the first group shall be presented with characters in bold style. The text messages of the second group shall be presented with characters in regular style. d) The text messages belonging to the same group shall be classified in a chronological way; the newest text message being displayed on top of the group. e) It shall be possible to scroll line by line through the list of text messages. The scrolling function shall not be circular i.e. the first line of the first text message shall not scroll to the last line of the last text message and vice-versa. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 85 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface f) When using touch screen technology, to scroll through the list of text messages the area E10 shall be dedicated to the [Up] button, the area E11 shall be dedicated to [Down] button. g) When using soft key technology, to scroll through the list of text messages the H5 shall be dedicated to the [Up] button and H6 shall be dedicated to the [Down] button. The symbols NA13, NA15 and NA14, NA16 shall echo the [Up] and [Down] buttons respectively in E10 and E11. h) Sound Sinfo, see chapter 14, shall be used when a new text message of the first group is displayed for the first time. No sound shall be used when a new text message of the second group is displayed for the first time.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.2.3.4.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.2.3.4.8, PDF p.86

8.2.3.4.8 The following applies only to text messages to be acknowledged regardless of the group they belong to: a) A text message to be acknowledged shall be presented alone (see Figure 63) (the other messages that do not have to be acknowledged are temporarily not shown) in the E5-E9 (touch screen technology) or E5-E8 (soft key technology) area. b) As long as an Ack is required, the requirements specified in 5.4 shall apply on the full area formed by E5-E9 (touch screen technology) or E5-E8 (soft key technology); E10 and E11 shall show respectively the symbols NA15 and NA16. c) After acknowledgement and if the acknowledgement does not lead to the end of display, the corresponding text message shall be managed as a text message that do not have to be acknowledged but without playing the sound Sinfo.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.3.7.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.3.7.5, PDF p.106

8.3.7.5 The PASP information shall only display up to 3 speed discontinuities more restrictive than the ceiling permitted speed at the current train front position and with a speed value greater than zero.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.3.7.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.3.7.6, PDF p.106

8.3.7.6 The fourth speed restriction shall be reserved for the first target at zero speed, if any.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.3.7.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.3.7.7, PDF p.106

8.3.7.7 The speed shall not be presented to scale, but with fixed ratios relative to the ceiling permitted speed at the current train front position (1/1). Speed decreases shall be shown as 3/4, 1/2 or 1/4 of the ceiling permitted speed at the current train position. Each time a speed decrease is effective, the width of the diagram shall be shorten by quarter(s) of the full width as follows (with regards to a percentage of the ceiling permitted speed at the current train front position): a) From 99% to 75%: 1/4 b) From 74% to 50%: 1/2 c) From 49% to 1%: 3/4

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.3.7.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.3.7.8, PDF p.106

8.3.7.8 Example: if the ceiling permitted speed at the current train front position is 140 km/h and the first speed reduction is 70 km/h, then the speed profile in D7 shows a reduction to 1/2 of the current maximum; if the next speed reduction is 40 km/h, then the speed profile in D7 shows 1/4 of the current maximum.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.3.7.9

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.3.7.9, PDF p.106

8.3.7.9 If a speed increase is drawn using symbol PL21, no further speed decrease except, if any, the speed decrease to the first target at zero speed shall be shown on the PASP in D7.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 8.3.7.10

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.3.7.10, PDF p.106

8.3.7.10 The background colour of the PASP in D7-D8 shall be ‘PASP dark’.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 8.3.7.11, PDF p.106

8.3.7.11 The PASP diagram colour shall be ‘PASP light’. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 106 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

9.1.1.1 The chapter 9 is applicable for the modes SN and NL in ERTMS/ETCS level NTC.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.1.1.2, PDF p.117

9.1.1.2 The chapter 9.2 applies regardless the National System is interfaced to the ERTMS/ETCS onboard through an STM. In case the National System is interfaced to the ERTMS/ETCS onboard through an STM, the chapters 9.3, 9.3.7.1.10 and 9.5 also apply.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.2.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.2.1.1, PDF p.117

9.2.1.1 The ETCS objects/functions in document [2] chapter 4.7.2, modes SN and NL shall be displayed as far as they concern a default window, i.e. the appearance shall be as specified in chapter 8 but the location of the ETCS objects/functions will be according to the definition of the NTC default window of the corresponding National System.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.2.1.2, PDF p.117

9.2.1.2 The ETCS buttons accessing the sub-level windows shall be available with the labels as specified in 8.5 but with their size and location depending on the ergonomic arrangements of areas of the NTC default window of the corresponding National System.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.1.1, PDF p.117

9.3.1.1 All texts used with NTC objects shall use the same font, indent, character and line spacing as used for ETCS objects.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.1.2, PDF p.117

9.3.2 Flashing mode and style

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.2.1, PDF p.117

9.3.2.1 When flashing style ‘yellow frame’ is selected, each NTC indicator or button requested to flash by the STM shall be surrounded by a flashing frame as specified in 5.1.1.3.1. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 117 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.2.2, PDF p.118

9.3.2.2 When flashing style ‘whole area’ is selected, each NTC indicator or button requested to flash by the STM shall toggle between visible and not visible state (i.e. the dark blue background colour).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.2.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.2.3, PDF p.118

9.3.2.3 Flashing of different objects shall be synchronised: all objects with normal flashing mode and the same frequency shall be in the same state at the same time; objects with counterphase flashing shall be in the alternative state at this time.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.3.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.3.1, PDF p.118

9.3.3.1 NTC text messages shall be treated and displayed as and together with ETCS text messages, including scrolling and acknowledgment (see 8.2.3.4).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.3.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.3.2, PDF p.118

9.3.3.2 Exception: the display shall be according to the display attribute sent by the STM with the text message.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.1, PDF p.118

9.3.4.1 An NTC indicator can display text and/or an icon. Its state may change by changing the contained text, icon, text colour, text background colour or flashing mode. Additionally its position may change.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.2, PDF p.118

9.3.4.2 Visibility of caption text

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.2.1, PDF p.118

9.3.4.2.1 The caption text shall always be visible when no icon is requested by the STM.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.2.2, PDF p.118

9.3.4.2.2 If the STM uses the customisable DMI, the caption text shall also be visible, if “display of text upon icon” is requested as corresponding icon attribute in the configuration data.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.2.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.2.3, PDF p.118

9.3.4.2.3 Otherwise the caption text shall be ignored by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.3, PDF p.118

9.3.4.3 An indicator shall be displayed according to the display attribute sent with the indicator request.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.4, PDF p.118

9.3.4.4 If both the caption text and the icon are displayed, the layering shall be text in foreground, icon in middle layer and background colour in background.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.4.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.4.5, PDF p.118

9.3.4.5 The part of the caption text from the seventh character shall be displayed on a second line.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.5.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.5.1, PDF p.118

9.3.5.1 Buttons are a pure functional extension of Indicators. All requirements of chapter 9.3.4 shall apply to buttons, by replacing "indicator" with "button".

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.5.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.5.2, PDF p.118

9.3.5.2 The ERTMS/ETCS-onboard shall display NTC buttons pressed and not pressed like ETCS buttons.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.6.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.6.1, PDF p.118

9.3.6.1 A sound shall be played according to the sound definition sent in the sound requests. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 118 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7, PDF p.119

9.3.7 Supervision Information

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1 If the STM uses the customisable DMI service and is configured to display such information or it uses the unified DMI service, the speed and distance supervision information sent by the STM shall be displayed by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board according to the following rules:

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.1, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.1 The current train speed pointer shall be displayed as specified in 8.2.1.2 but with the colour requested for it by the STM.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.2, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.2 The current train speed digital shall be displayed as specified in 8.2.1.3.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.3, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.3 When requested by the display mode sent by the STM, the distance to target bar shall be displayed as specified in 8.2.2.1.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.4, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.4 When requested by the display mode sent by the STM, the distance to target digital shall be displayed as specified in 8.2.2.2.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.5, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.5 When the supervision speeds are requested to be displayed as bars, the width of those speed bars shall be 9 cells, except for: a) the part of the permitted speed bar below a release speed bar, b) the release speed bar, c) the intervention speed bar if it is requested to display it with the “wide bar width”.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.6, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.6 When a release speed bar is displayed, the permitted speed bar and the release speed bar shall be indicated applying clause 8.2.1.6.4 by analogy to the CSG.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.7, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.7 When the intervention speed bar is requested to be displayed with “wide bar width”, it shall be displayed with 20 cells.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.8, PDF p.119

9.3.7.1.8 The speed bars and hooks shall be displayed along the speed dial in the area B2 as for the Circular speed gauge and for the Basic speed hook(s) used on the ETCS default window, except consideration of the display mode. a) A dark grey bar below 0km/h (-149 degrees to -144 degrees, as specified for ETCS default window) if display of any bar is requested. b) The target speed bar in the colour requested for target speed between permitted speed and target speed if permitted speed is displayed and is lower than target speed, otherwise between 0km/h and target speed. c) If the requested display mode is ‘hook only’, the target speed hook shall be displayed at the target speed as specified in 8.2.1.5.5 but with the colour requested for it by the STM. d) If the requested display mode is ‘hook and bar’, the target speed hook shall be displayed at the target speed as specified in 8.2.1.4.7 but with the colour requested for it by the STM. e) The permitted speed bar in the colour requested for permitted speed between target speed and permitted speed if target speed is displayed and is lower than permitted Version 3.6.0 PAGE 119 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface speed, otherwise between 0km/h and permitted speed. The permitted speed bar may overlap with the release speed bar. f) If the requested display mode is ‘hook only’, the permitted speed hook shall be displayed at the permitted speed as specified in 8.2.1.5.4 but with the colour requested for it by the STM. g) If the requested display mode is ‘hook and bar’, the permitted speed hook shall be displayed at the permitted speed as specified in 8.2.1.4.7 but with the colour requested for it by the STM. h) The intervention speed bar between permitted speed and intervention speed in the colour requested for intervention speed. i) The release speed bar between 0km/h and release speed, possibly overlapping with permitted speed bar in the colour requested for the release speed. j) The order of superimposing objects on top of the background from back to front is: intervention speed bar, target speed bar/hook, permitted speed bar/hook, release speed bar.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.9

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.9, PDF p.120

9.3.7.1.9 The release speed digital display shall be displayed in the colour requested for the release speed.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.3.7.1.10

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.3.7.1.10, PDF p.120

9.3.7.1.10 As long as no information has been sent by the STM, the train speed pointer shall be displayed in grey and no other supervision information shall be displayed.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.4, PDF p.120

9.4 Customisable DMI service

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.4.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.4.1.1, PDF p.120

9.4.1.1 The size and position of NTC DMI objects shall be specified in cells using the same coordinate system with 640x480 cells as specified in 6.2. The position of an object shall be defined as the offset of the upper left corner of the object from the upper left corner of the total grid array. It shall be retrieved from the configuration data using the position identifier sent by the STM. The specification of the customisable DMI service consequently does not reuse the ETCS layout except when explicitly referring to the name of an ETCS area.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.4.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.4.1.2, PDF p.120

9.4.1.2 With the customisable DMI service, the areas for text message (E5-E11) and for its related buttons shall not be used for DMI elements by an STM other than its national text messages. If the ETCS speed and supervision display is used by the STM, it shall not be hidden by other NTC elements displayed in the same area.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.4.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.4.1.3, PDF p.120

9.4.1.3 The customisable DMI service shall display icons centred in the specified area.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.1.1, PDF p.120

9.5.1.1 As a principle for the unified DMI service, the ETCS default window is offered to the STMs with the same definition of the areas as specified in chapter 6. No ETCS areas are moved. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 120 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.1.2, PDF p.121

9.5.1.2 Only areas of the ETCS default window that are not used for ETCS information in NTC levels and modes NL or SN can be used for NTC buttons and indicators.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.1.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.1.2.1, PDF p.121

9.5.1.2.1 The available areas for buttons are a) For soft key technology: F8, F9, F10, H2, H3, H4 b) For touch screen technology: F8, F9,C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, G1-G101

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.1.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.1.2.2, PDF p.121

9.5.1.2.2 The available areas for indicators are B3, B4, B5, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, G1-G101, and H1 for soft key technology.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.1.3, PDF p.121

9.5.1.3 The available button and indicator areas are mapped to a corresponding position identifier.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.1.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.1.4, PDF p.121

9.5.1.4 Since the unified DMI has no configuration for the display of national information, the following restrictions apply: a) NTC indicators and buttons are displayed with caption texts, text and background colour, but without icons. The font size and text alignment cannot be selected. b) The flashing style used for NTC indicators/buttons and the slow/fast flashing frequencies cannot be selected. c) NTC sounds are specified by a sequence of segments defined by a duration and an associated frequency sent to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board. d) The speed dial range in B0 is the same range as the ETCS one.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.2.1, PDF p.121

9.5.2.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall display buttons and indicators in the ETCS area specified by the position identifier.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.2.2, PDF p.121

9.5.2.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall display caption texts of buttons and indicators with 10 cells font size and centred vertically and horizontally.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.2.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.2.3, PDF p.121

9.5.2.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board shall implement the flashing style as ‘yellow frame’ for the NTC indicators and buttons requested to flash by the STM. For slow flashing the frame shall toggle every 0.5 seconds, for fast flashing every 0.25 seconds.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 9.5.2.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 9.5.2.4, PDF p.121

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.4, PDF p.124

10.3.1.4 When using the soft key technology, the width of the total input field shall be 266 cells.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.4.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.4.1, PDF p.124

10.3.1.4.1 For soft key technology, the input fields will be located on the D/G/I area (having a width of 266 cells).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.5, PDF p.124

10.3.1.5 Each input field shall be divided into a label area and a data area.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.6, PDF p.124

10.3.1.6 The label area shall give the topic of the input field.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.7, PDF p.124

10.3.1.7 Exception: If there is only one input field within the window, the input field can only consist of a data area. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 124 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.7.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.7.1, PDF p.125

10.3.1.7.1 Note: With a single input field, the window title can already indicate unambiguously the topic of the input field.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.8, PDF p.125

10.3.1.8 When the input field contains a label area, the width of the data area shall be 102 cells.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.9

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.9, PDF p.125

10.3.1.9 The label area shall be placed to the left of the data area.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.10

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.10, PDF p.125

10.3.1.10 The text in the label area shall be aligned to the right of the label area with an indent of 10 cells.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.11

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.11, PDF p.125

10.3.1.11 The value of the data in the data area shall be aligned to the left of the data area with an indent of 10 cells.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.12

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.12, PDF p.125

10.3.1.12 The text colour of the label area shall be grey; the background colour of the label area shall be dark grey.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.13

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.13, PDF p.125

10.3.1.13 If the input field is not selected and no data value has been accepted yet by the driver during the data entry / validation process (i.e. ‘not selected’ state), the background colour of the data area shall be dark grey and, if any, the data value colour shall be grey.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.13.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.13.1, PDF p.125

10.3.1.13.1 Note: regarding the definition of a data entry / validation process; see chapter 10.6.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.14

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.14, PDF p.125

10.3.1.14 If the input field is selected (i.e. ‘selected’ state), the background colour of the data area shall be medium grey and the colour of the data value or of the value corresponding to the pressed key(s) (see 10.3.1.19) shall be black.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.15

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.15, PDF p.125

10.3.1.15 If the input field is not selected but a data value has already been accepted by the driver during the data entry / validation process (i.e. ‘accepted’ state), the background colour of the data area shall be dark grey and the the data value colour shall be white.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.16

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.16, PDF p.125

10.3.1.16 Table 21 gives an overview of the data field states. Not selected Selected Accepted Background of the dark grey medium grey dark grey data area Data value grey black white Value corresponding - black - to the pressed key(s) (see 10.3.1.19) Table 21 – Overview of data field states

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.18

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.18, PDF p.126

10.3.1.18 When an input field is selected, the associated keyboard shall be presented in the area below the area of the input field(s).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.19

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.19, PDF p.126

10.3.1.19 After the first press on a data key of the associated keyboard, the value corresponding to the pressed data key shall be displayed in the data area instead of the data value (if any) of the selected input field.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.20

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.20, PDF p.126

10.3.1.20 If the input field is not selected anymore whilst a value has been entered / modified without accepting it, the entered value shall be erased from the data area and the current data value (if any) shall be deleted.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.21

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.21, PDF p.126

10.3.1.21 To accept the entered value in an input field in order that it replaces the current data value (if any), the driver shall activate the associated [Enter] button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.22

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.22, PDF p.126

10.3.1.22 When using the touch screen technology, the associated [Enter] button shall be the data field itself.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.23

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.23, PDF p.126

10.3.1.23 When a data entry / validation process starts, the first input field shall be in the ‘selected’ state, all other input fields shall be in the ‘not selected’ state. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 126 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.24

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.24, PDF p.127

10.3.1.24 After activating the [Enter] button associated to the selected input field, this input field shall go to the ‘accepted’ state and the next input field related to the same topic (i.e. which can be on a next data entry window) shall be selected automatically.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.25

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.25, PDF p.127

10.3.1.25 The list of input fields of the data entry window(s) related to the same topic shall be circular i.e. the first input field follows the last one and the last input field preceeds the first one.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.26

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.26, PDF p.127

10.3.1.26 When using the touch screen technology, it shall be possible for the driver to select a specific input field by activating the input field area (the label or data part). For the activation, the input field shall behave like an up-type button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.1.27

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.1.27, PDF p.127

10.3.1.27 When using soft key technology, it shall be possible for the driver to select a specific input field by using the [Up] and [Down] scroll buttons.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.2, PDF p.127

10.3.2 Entering characters

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.2.1, PDF p.127

10.3.2.1 A cursor shall be used to indicate to the driver where his next selected character will be inserted within the input field.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.2.2, PDF p.127

10.3.2.2 The cursor shall be a horizontal line below the position of the next character to be entered i.e. an underscore.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.2.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.2.3, PDF p.127

10.3.2.3 The cursor shall flash by changing from visible to not visible (e.g. background colour) with a nominal frequency of 2 Hz with a symmetrical mark space ratio.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.2.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.2.4, PDF p.127

10.3.2.4 When a data key of a keyboard allows entering one single character (e.g. all data keys of a numeric keyboard), the cursor shall jump to the next position in the input field as soon as this data key entry is echoed within the input field.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.2.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.2.5, PDF p.127

10.3.2.5 When a data key of a keyboard allows entering various characters (e.g. all data keys of an alphanumeric keyboard), the following shall apply: a) the cursor shall jump automatically with a delay-time of 2 s to the next position in the input field after displaying this data key entry within the input field. b) by pressing the same data key again within these 2 s delay-time or by holding the data key for some time, another character under the same data key shall be selected; c) by pressing another data key within these 2 s delay-time the cursor shall be forced to jump to the next position in the input field directly.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.2.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.2.6, PDF p.127

10.3.2.6 The rules specified in 5.1.5 shall apply as soon as the 6th character of an alphanumeric or numeric data is entered.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.1, PDF p.127

10.3.3.1 An echo text shall be composed of a label part and a data part.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.2, PDF p.127

10.3.3.2 The label part shall be identical to the label of the concerned input field.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.3, PDF p.127

10.3.3.3 The data part of the echo text shall display the data value of the concerned input field. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 127 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.4, PDF p.128

10.3.3.4 Exception: If the data value is not consistent, the data part of the echo text shall indicate the type of inconsistency as specified in 10.3.4 instead of the data value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.5, PDF p.128

10.3.3.5 The echo text shall be white if the entered data has been accepted by the driver during the data entry / validation process, otherwise it shall be grey.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.6, PDF p.128

10.3.3.6 The echo texts shall be presented inside the A/B/C/E area in the same order as their related input fields in D/F/G (touch screen technology) or D/G/I (soft key technology).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.7, PDF p.128

10.3.3.7 The labels of the echo texts shall be right aligned with an indent of 5 on the left side of the X position 204.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.8

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.8, PDF p.128

10.3.3.8 The label of the first echo text shall be 112 cells (i.e. an indent of 100 cells + the 12 cells of the character size) below the top of area A/B/C/E.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.9

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.9, PDF p.128

10.3.3.9 The data of the echo texts shall be left aligned with an indent of 5 cells on the right side of the X position 204.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.3.10

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.3.10, PDF p.128

10.3.3.10 The data of the first echo text shall be 112 cells (i.e. an indent of 100 cells + the 12 cells of the character size) below the top of area A/B/C/E.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.1.1, PDF p.128

10.3.4.1.1 This chapter defines the mechanisms used to inform the driver about data entry mistakes. For that purpose, five types of checks are defined: a) Technical range check used when the value of an input field is out of its technical range (e.g. outside the range defined in document [2], section A.3.11), b) Technical resolution check used when the value of an input field is not matching its resolution (e.g. different from the resolution defined in document [2], section A.3.11) c) Technical cross-check used when the values of several input fields do not technically fit together, d) Operational range check used when the value of an input field is out of its operational range (e.g. outside the range used for the nominal operational situations), e) Operational cross-check used when the values of several input fields do not operationally fit together.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.1.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.1.1.1, PDF p.128

10.3.4.1.1.1 Note: The main difference between the technical and operational rules is that an operational one can be overruled by the driver while a technical one forces him to modify the data value(s).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.1.2, PDF p.128

10.3.4.1.2 It shall be possible to configure in the on-board the permitted range(s), resolution for a specific input field as well as the cross-check rules between several input fields. However, the definitions of those rules are outside the scope of this specification.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.1.3, PDF p.128

10.3.4.1.3 Since these mechanisms rely on the echo texts, it is only possible to inform the driver about data entry mistakes in data entry windows with echo texts. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 128 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.2, PDF p.129

10.3.4.2 Technical range checks

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.2.1, PDF p.129

10.3.4.2.1 The check versus the technical permitted range shall take place when an entered data value is accepted by the driver.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.2.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.2.2, PDF p.129

10.3.4.2.2 When the entered data value of an input field is outside its pre-configured technical permitted range, the data part of its echo text shall indicate ‘++++’ in red.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.2.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.2.3, PDF p.129

10.3.4.2.3 The input field that contains the out of range shall remain in the “Selected IF/data value” state (see Figure 97) and shall still show the entered data value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.2.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.2.4, PDF p.129

10.3.4.2.4 The [Enter] button and, if any, the [Up], [Down], [Next] and [Previous] navigation buttons shall be disabled until the state of the input field switches to “Selected IF/value of pressed key(s)”.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.3, PDF p.129

10.3.4.3 Technical resolution checks

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.3.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.3.1, PDF p.129

10.3.4.3.1 The check versus the technical resolution shall take place when an entered data value is accepted by the driver.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.3.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.3.2, PDF p.129

10.3.4.3.2 When an entered data value of an input field is outside its pre-configured technical resolution, the data part of its echo text shall indicate ‘++++’ in red.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.3.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.3.3, PDF p.129

10.3.4.3.3 The input field that contains the wrong resolution shall remain in the “Selected IF/data value” state (see Figure 97) and shall still show the entered data value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.3.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.3.4, PDF p.129

10.3.4.3.4 The [Enter] button and, if any, the [Up], [Down], [Next] and [Previous] navigation buttons shall be disabled until the state of the input field switches to “Selected IF/value of pressed key(s)”.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.4, PDF p.129

10.3.4.4 Technical cross-checks

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.4.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.4.1, PDF p.129

10.3.4.4.1 When a valid button activation is performed on the ‘Yes’ button attached to the question ‘[Window Title] entry complete?’ (see 10.3.4.5 and 10.3.6), the technical cross-check rules shall be executed in sequence.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.4.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.4.2, PDF p.129

10.3.4.4.2 For the input fields whose entered data values do not comply with the currently executed cross-check rule, the data part of their corresponding echo texts shall indicate ‘????’ in red.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.4.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.4.3, PDF p.129

10.3.4.4.3 The input fields not complying with the cross-check rule shall still show their entered data value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.4.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.4.4, PDF p.129

10.3.4.4.4 The ‘Yes’ button button attached to the question ‘[Window Title] entry complete?’ shall be disabled until one of the entered data values is modified i.e. until one of the input field switches to “Not Selected IF/Accepted Data value” (see Figure 97).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.5, PDF p.129

10.3.4.5 Operational range checks

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.5.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.5.1, PDF p.129

10.3.4.5.1 The check versus the operational permitted range shall take place when an entered data value is accepted by the driver and only if the technical range check, if any, is satisfied. Version 3.6.0 PAGE 129 OF 263 ERA ERTMS unit ETCS Driver Machine Interface

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.5.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.5.2, PDF p.130

10.3.4.5.2 When the entered data value of the input field is outside its pre-configured operational range, the data part of its echo text shall indicate ‘++++’ in yellow.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.5.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.5.3, PDF p.130

10.3.4.5.3 The input field that contains the operational out of range shall remain in the“Selected IF/data value” state (see Figure 97) and shall still show the entered data value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.5.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.5.4, PDF p.130

10.3.4.5.4 If any, the [Up], [Down], [Next] and [Previous] navigation buttons shall be disabled until the state of the input field switches to “Selected IF/value of pressed key(s)”.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.5.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.5.5, PDF p.130

10.3.4.5.5 The [Enter] button shall become a delay-type button to allow the driver to overrule the operational range check rule.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.5.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.5.6, PDF p.130

10.3.4.5.6 If the driver performs a valid button activation on the delay-type [Enter] button, the entered data value of the input field shall be considered as permitted meaning that the input field shall go in the “Not Selected IF/Accepted Data value” state and the data part of the echo text shall display the entered data value instead of ‘++++’.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.6, PDF p.130

10.3.4.6 Operational cross-checks

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.6.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.6.1, PDF p.130

10.3.4.6.1 When a valid button activation is performed on the ‘Yes’ button attached to the question ‘[Window Title] entry complete?’ (see 10.3.4.5 and 10.3.6), the operational cross-check rules shall be executed in sequence and only if all technical cross-check(s) is/are satisfied.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.6.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.6.2, PDF p.130

10.3.4.6.2 For the input fields whose entered data values do not comply with the currently executed cross-check rule, the data part of their corresponding echo texts shall indicate ‘????’ in yellow.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.6.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.6.3, PDF p.130

10.3.4.6.3 The input fields not complying with the cross-check rule shall still show their entered data value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.6.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.6.4, PDF p.130

10.3.4.6.4 The ‘Yes’ button attached to the question ‘[Window Title] entry complete?’ shall become a delay-type button to allow the driver to overrule the operational cross-check rule.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.4.6.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.4.6.5, PDF p.130

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.5.18, PDF p.134

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.5.19, PDF p.134

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.6.22

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.6.22, PDF p.138

10.3.6.22 When a dedicated keyboard with predefined choices is presented, the following shall apply: a) The window shall contain a list of selections (texts) in area D/G/I. b) The list shall be displayed left aligned with an indent of 15 cells from the left of the area D/G/I. c) The first selection of the list shall be 27 cells (i.e. an indent of 15 cells + the 12 cells of the character size) below the position of the input field 3 (half grid array) or input field 4 (total grid array). d) The text of each selection shall:  start with a number or a letter giving the position of the selection in the list;  identify the name/value of the selection;  separate the number/letter and the name/value of the selection by a ‘-‘. e) The numbers or letters used for the selections shall be positioned in a logical order respectively from 1 to maximum 10 or from A to J; f) The labels of the F buttons shall be numbers/letters matching the numbers/letters of the selection/value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.6.22.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.6.22.1, PDF p.138

10.3.6.22.1 Exception: When a dedicated keyboard is limited to a ‘No’/’Yes’ choice, no list of selections shall be presented in D/G/I area. F7 shall be the ‘No’ key and F8 shall be the ‘Yes’ key.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.3.6.22.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.3.6.22.2, PDF p.138

10.3.6.22.2 When more than 10 predefined choices exist for a dedicated keyboard, 10.3.6.22 shall apply for each group of maximum 9 choices and F10 shall be dedicated to the [More] button. When pressing the [More] button, the next (maximum) 9 predefined choices shall be presented but with the numbers/letters adapted accordingly (e.g. going respectively from 10 to maximum 18 or from J to maximum R for the next 9 choices). The list of predefined choices shall be circular i.e. the 1st group of predefined choices (from 1 to 9) follows the last group of predefined choices.

10.6 Data entry / validation process

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.6.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.6.1.1, PDF p.146

10.6.1.1 If not started yet, a data entry / validation process regarding a topic shall start when the first data entry window of this topic is displayed.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.6.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.6.1.2, PDF p.146

10.6.1.2 If no validation window regarding the same topic as the data entry window exists, the data entry / validation process shall stop: a) when one of the data entry window(s) is left by accepting the data values via the ‘Yes’ button, or b) when any of the data entry window(s) is left via the [Close] button, or c) when any of the data entry window(s) is left due to another reason.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 10.6.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 10.6.1.3, PDF p.146

10.6.1.3 If a validation window regarding the same topic as the data entry window exists, the data entry / validation process shall stop: a) when the validation window is left by accepting a data value set to ‘Yes’ in its input field, or b) when any of the data entry window(s) is left via the [Close] button, or c) when the validation window is left via the [Close] button, or d) when any of the data entry window(s) is left due to a reason other than accepting the data values via the ‘Yes’ button, or e) when the validation window is left due to another reason. ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.6, PDF p.170

11.3.9.6 It shall be possible to select by means of an input signal from the train interface the kind of train data entry configuration to be applied amongst the following possibilities: a) Fixed train data entry: the Train data window shall contain only one input field allowing the driver to enter a train type amongst a number of pre-configured ones. Each train type shall represent a combination of all train data. Once a train type is selected, the onboard shall not offer any possibility for the driver to change any value of a specific train data composing the selected train type. b) Flexible train data entry: the Train data entry window(s) shall contain one or more input fields for the specific train data the driver has to enter/modify. c) Switchable train data entry: the Train data entry window(s) shall offer the possibility to switch from a “Fixed train data entry” layout to a “Flexible train data entry” layout or vice versa.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7 Requirements applicable to “Switchable train data entry”:

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7.1, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7.1 The Train data window(s) shall by default be presented with the layout lastly used, i.e. the layout “Fixed train data entry” or “Flexible train data entry” shall always be retained.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7.2, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7.2 The Train data window(s) shall present an enabled ‘switch’ button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7.3, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7.3 When the driver presses the ‘switch’ button, the Train data window(s) shall switch to the other layout, i.e. to “Fixed train data entry” if the current layout is “Flexible train data entry” or vice versa.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7.4, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7.4 The label of the ‘switch’ button shall be ‘Select type’ if the Train data window(s) show a “Flexible train data entry” layout or with the label ‘Enter data’ if the Train data window(s) show a “Fixed train data entry” layout.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7.5, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7.5 The ‘switch’ button shall be positioned: a) For touch screen technology: in the bottom right corner of D/F/G area with a size of 60 x 50 cells (w x h) i.e. at the position (246,400), b) For soft key technology: in the D/G/I area and above F9 with a size of 64 x 50 cells (w x h) (i.e. at the position (178,400). The text label of the ‘switch’ button shall be in black. The background colour shall be in medium grey. The ‘switch’ button shall have the same border as an input field applying 5.1.1.1.4.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7.6, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7.6 For soft key technology, when the ‘switch’ button is enabled, an associated soft key with the same label as the ‘switch’ button shall be presented in F9 if the [Down] button has been pressed being on the last input field or the [Up] button has been pressed being on the first input field.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.3.9.7.6.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.3.9.7.6.1, PDF p.170

11.3.9.7.6.1 Note: the ‘switch’ button is consequently inserted between the last and the first input fields within the circular list of input fields (see 10.3.1.25).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.1, PDF p.195

11.7.1.1 In a dialogue sequence, the latest active window including the mentioned configuration of objects/symbols (e.g. the main window with all buttons disabled and the hour glass symbol ST05 displayed) shall remain displayed until another window or another configuration of the same window is mentioned further on in the flowchart.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.2, PDF p.195

11.7.1.2 When an event involves a driver’s action on a button, it assumes that the corresponding button is enabled (see 11.1 for the conditions enabling a button).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.3

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.3, PDF p.195

11.7.1.3 The status of data mentioned in the dialogue sequences refers to the status of data stored onboard as defined in document [2].

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.4

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.4, PDF p.195

11.7.1.4 If the status is “invalid” or “valid”, the value stored onboard shall be presented to the driver when entering the corresponding data entry window.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.4.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.4.1, PDF p.195

11.7.1.4.1 Exception: for the train data windows; see S3-1 of the main dialogue sequence. For the train data validation window; see S3-2 of the main dialogue sequence.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.5

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.5, PDF p.195

11.7.1.5 For a window covering the half grid array, the value stored onboard shall be replaced by the data value of the input field when the driver accepts this data value.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.6

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.6, PDF p.195

11.7.1.6 For a window covering the total grid array, the values stored onboard shall be replaced by the data values of the input fields when the driver presses the ‘Yes’ button.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.6.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.6.1, PDF p.195

11.7.1.6.1 Exception: for the train data windows, the values stored onboard shall be replaced by the values of the input fields for train data only when the train data validation window is left with the value of its input field set to ‘Yes’. It means that no action is done on the train data stored onboard when the driver presses the ‘Yes’ button of the train data windows (see S3-2 of the main window dialogue sequence).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.6.2

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.6.2, PDF p.195

11.7.1.6.2 Exception: for the Set VBC or Remove VBC window, the action on the VBCs stored onboard shall be performed respectively with the value of the input field ‘VBC set code’ or of the input field ‘VBC remove code’ only when the corresponding validation window is left with the value of its input field set to ‘Yes’. It means that no action is done on the VBCs stored onboard when the driver presses the ‘Yes’ button of the Set VBC or Remove VBC window (see S6-2 and S7-2 of the settings dialogue sequence).

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.1.7

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.7, PDF p.195

11.7.1.7 After the Start Up dialogue sequence (see 11.7.2), if one of the windows mentioned in Table 48 is currently displayed and any of the enabling conditions (see 11.2) of the corresponding button is not fulfilled anymore, the data entry / validation process shall be stopped and the parent window shall be displayed instead. 11.7.1.8 During the Start Up dialogue sequence, if a driver’s acknowledgement is required, it shall be displayed 1 second after the end of the Start Up dialogue sequence.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.1.9, PDF p.196

11.7.1.9 After the Start Up dialogue sequence, if a data entry or validation window is currently displayed when a driver’s acknowledgement is required, the data entry / validation process shall be stopped, the parent window shall be displayed instead and the driver’s acknowledgement shall appear 1 second afterwards.

11.7.2.1 The “Start Up” dialogue sequence shall guide the driver when a start of mission is initiated as specified in [2] chapter 5.4.

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.2.1.1, PDF p.196

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.2.2, PDF p.196

11.7.2.2 The [close] button shall be disabled in all windows presented before reaching S10 except in the steps S1-1, S1-2, S3-2-2 and S3-3.

ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0 — clause 11.7.2.2.1

Citation: ERA_ERTMS_015560 v3.6.0, clause 11.7.2.2.1, PDF p.196

11.7.2.2.1 Note: In S10, the driver can therefore close the start up dialogue sequence to go to another sub-level window e.g. to go to the Override window and press the EOA button (if enabled).

This procedure shall go to S10.
