5.6 Shunting Initiated by Driver

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.1.1, PDF p.24

5.6.1.1 The procedure describes the selection of shunting by the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.1.2, PDF p.24

5.6.1.2 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.2, PDF p.24

5.6.2 Table of requirements for “Shunting Initiated by Driver” procedure

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.2.1, PDF p.24

5.6.2.1 The ID numbers in the table are used for the representation of the procedure in form of a flowchart in section 5.6.3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.2.2, PDF p.24

5.6.2.2 Procedure ID # Requirements E015 The train is at standstill and the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is in FS, LS, OS, SR, SN, UN or PT mode or is in SB mode with necessary preconditions fulfilled (Driver ID known, Level known,... see procedure "Start of mission"). When the driver selects Shunting (E015) the process shall go to D020. D020 If the current ETCS Level of operation is 0 or 1, the process shall go to A050. If the current ETCS Level of operation is 2 or 3, the process shall go to A045. If the current ETCS Level of operation is NTC, the process shall go to D030 D030 If there is an ongoing National Trip procedure reported by the STM, the process shall go to A030 Otherwise the process shall go to A050 A030 The process shall go to the “Train trip" procedure A045 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall send the “Request for Shunting” message to the RBC together with a position report (with special value “position unknown” if the position is not known) The process shall go to S050. S050 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment awaits the reply to the SH request. If SH authorised is received from the RBC (optionally with a list of balise groups for SH area, which the train can pass when the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment is in shunting mode) (E090), the process shall go to A050. If “SH refused” is received from the RBC (E215), the process shall go to A220.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.24

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP ID # Requirements A050 The mode shall change to SH. Any previous list of balise groups for SH area shall be deleted or replaced by a new list of balise groups for SH area. The process shall go to D040. D040 If there is an ongoing mission, the process shall go to A100. If there is no ongoing mission, the process shall go to D080. A100 The process shall go to the “End of Mission" procedure D080 If the current ETCS Level of operation is 2 or 3, the process shall go to A095. If the current ETCS Level of operation is 0, 1 or NTC the process shall END. A095 The mode change shall be reported to the RBC. The process shall go to S100. S100 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment awaits the RBC order to terminate the communication session. When an order to terminate the communication session is received from RBC the process shall go to A115. A115 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall terminate the communication session. The process shall END. A220 An indication shall be given to the driver that SH was refused by the RBC. The process shall END.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.4.1, PDF p.26

5.6.4.1 ERTMS/ETCS level 2 or 3: no answer to Shunting request is received from the RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.4.1.1, PDF p.26

5.6.4.1.1 In case a communication session is established and no reply is received from the RBC within a fixed waiting time (see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data) after sending the “Request for Shunting” message, the message shall be repeated with the fixed waiting time after each repetition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.26

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.4.1.2, PDF p.27

5.6.4.1.2 After a defined number of repetitions (see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data), and if no reply is received within the fixed waiting time from the time of the last sending of “Request for Shunting”, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall inform the driver and shall terminate the communication session.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.4.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.4.1.3, PDF p.27

5.6.4.1.3 If no authorisation for SH mode can be received from the RBC, refer to procedure “Override”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.4.2, PDF p.27

5.6.4.2 ERTMS/ETCS level 2 or 3: in case a communication session is established and no order to terminate the session is received from the RBC within a fixed waiting time (see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data) after reporting the mode change, the report shall be repeated with the fixed waiting time after each repetition

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.6.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.6.4.3, PDF p.27

5.6.4.3 After a defined number of repetitions (see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data), and if no reply is received within the fixed waiting time from the last sending of the mode change report, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall terminate the communication session.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7, PDF p.28

5.7 Entry in Shunting with Order from Trackside

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.1, PDF p.28

5.7.1 General Requirements

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.1.1, PDF p.28

5.7.1.1 This procedure is used to allow the entry of a train into a shunting area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.1.2, PDF p.28

5.7.1.2 Note: The shunting area, possibly including a “safety envelope”, can be already occupied by shunting units, not controlled by the trackside. It is therefore possible that the train shall enter into the shunting area in OS mode. The switch to OS is performed according to the relevant procedure.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.1.3, PDF p.28

5.7.1.3 The order to switch to SH mode shall be given by means of a mode profile, optionally with a list of balises groups, which the train can pass when the ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment is in shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.1.4, PDF p.28

5.7.1.4 The switch to shunting, if the transition to shunting was ordered by trackside, requires a driver acknowledgement, according to the specifications below.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.1.5, PDF p.28

5.7.1.5 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has switched to Shunting mode, End of Mission, according to chapter 5.5.2.3, is performed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.2, PDF p.28

5.7.2 Shunting is requested for the current location (from modes different from Stand By and Post Trip)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.2.1, PDF p.28

5.7.2.1 In a level 1 area, or at the border from a level 0 to a level 1 area, the beginning of the shunting area can be the location where a balise group is installed. In level 2/3 it is possible to send an ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment the order to switch to shunting at the current location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.2.2, PDF p.28

5.7.2.2 Shunting is requested for the current location means that, according to the mode profile received the max safe front end of the train is at or in advance of the location for which switching to SH mode is requested.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.2.3, PDF p.28

5.7.2.3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch immediately to SH mode and a request for acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.2.4, PDF p.28

5.7.2.4 If the driver does not acknowledge within the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A.3.1) after the change to SH mode, the service brake command shall be triggered. The command shall be released as soon as the driver acknowledges (unless the command was triggered also for other reasons).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3, PDF p.28

5.7.3 Shunting is requested for a further location

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3.1, PDF p.28

5.7.3.1 An order to switch to SH at a further location can be sent a) in a level 1 area by a balise group,

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.28

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP b) in a level 2 or 3 area by the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3.2, PDF p.29

5.7.3.2 A request for acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver, when the following two conditions are fulfilled: a) the distance between the estimated front end of the train and the beginning of shunting area is shorter than a value, contained in the mode profile b) the speed is lower than the Shunting mode speed limit (National Value, or value given in the mode profile)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3.3, PDF p.29

5.7.3.3 Once the request for acknowledgement is displayed, it shall not be taken back, even if the above conditions are no more fulfilled (e.g., the train accelerates).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3.4, PDF p.29

5.7.3.4 Until the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has switched to SH mode, the beginning of the shunting area shall be considered as the EOA (instead of the EOA/LOA derived from the MA) and the SvL (with no release speed) shall be determined according to the mode profile either: a) as the SvL derived from the MA. In case the MA defines an LOA, the SvL shall be derived as if no LOA had been given. OR b) as the beginning of the shunting area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3.5, PDF p.29

5.7.3.5 When the driver acknowledges, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately switch to SH mode (refer to chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3.6, PDF p.29

5.7.3.6 If the max safe front end of the train reaches the beginning of the shunting area according the mode profile and the driver has not yet acknowledged, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch immediately to SH mode and a request for acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.3.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.3.7, PDF p.29

5.7.3.7 If, in this case, the driver does not acknowledge within the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A.3.1) after the change to SH mode, the service brake command shall be triggered. The command shall be released as soon as the driver acknowledges (unless the command was triggered also for other reasons).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.4, PDF p.29

5.7.4 Shunting from Stand By or Post Trip mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.4.1, PDF p.29

5.7.4.1 When performing a SoM or a Train Trip procedure and when the current level is 2 or 3, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment can receive a mode profile giving an Shunting area which the train has already entered with its max safe front end. In this case, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall first require an acknowledgement from the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.4.2, PDF p.29

5.7.4.2 When the driver acknowledges, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform transition to Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.29

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.7.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.7.5, PDF p.30

5.7.5 Flowchart mode is FS, LS, OS, SR, SB, PT, UN, or SN A mode profile for SH area has been received and is used Max safe front Beginning of Transition to FS/LS/OS mode further location inside SH area SH area (if not yet in FS/LS/OS) Max safe front overpasses begin of SH area - Start of SH mode profile Mode is SB YES supervised as EoA or PT - Waiting estimated front and speed in acknowledgement window NO - acknowledgement is Transition to requested to driver SH mode - Waiting for driver ackno Max safe front overpasses begin of SH area Driver acknowledges Transition to - acknowledgement is Driver acknowledges SH mode requested to driver within 5sec - Waiting for driver ackno 5 sec are elapsed & no ack by driver Service brake command until driver acknowledges Figure 3: Flowchart for “Entry in Shunting with Order from Trackside”

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.30

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.1, PDF p.31

5.8.1.1 In specific degraded situations (for example in the case of a failed signal, failed track circuit, failed point…), railways allow a train to pass its End of Movement Authority.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.2, PDF p.31

5.8.1.2 For ERTMS/ETCS, passing an End of Movement Authority can be required in degraded situations, e.g.  In level 2/3, if a train is stopped without MA in a location where radio is unavailable (e.g. after having received an emergency message, or after a train trip).  In level 2/3, if a train is stopped at the border between two adjacent RBCs (e.g. the interface between RBCs is unavailable).  In level 2/3, if a train is stopped after having passed the border between two adjacent RBCs (e.g. the connection to the Accepting RBC cannot be established).  In level 2/3, if the RBC is unable to give a permission to run (e.g. lost connection with the interlocking)  In level 1, if a signal cannot show a proceed aspect (e.g., signal failure, route cannot be set)  In level 1, if a train is stopped without MA (e.g. after the MA has been shortened due to a time-out).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.3, PDF p.31

5.8.1.3 In level 0/NTC areas, passing a signal at danger is only a national procedure. The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is not involved in this procedure, since it does not supervise the train movements.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.4, PDF p.31

5.8.1.4 In ERTMS equipped areas (level 1, 2 or 3), locations where the train shall stop are supervised by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment. Receiving an order from the signalman to pass the End of Movement Authority, the driver must then be able to inhibit this supervision.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.4.1, PDF p.31

5.8.1.4.1 Note: The driver must not use the “Override” procedure unless authorised by trackside personnel. This authorisation is covered by operational procedures.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.5, PDF p.31

5.8.1.5 If a signal at danger must be passed between announcement and execution of the level transition from an unfitted area (level 0) or from an area fitted with a National System (level NTC) to an ERTMS equipped area (level 1, 2, 3), the signalman gives the order to the driver to select “override”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.6, PDF p.31

5.8.1.6 Note: By using this procedure the driver is fully responsible for the train driving. Therefore Staff Responsible mode is entered when the driver selects “override”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.7, PDF p.31

5.8.1.7 In addition the procedure allows to avoid a train trip when passing a balise group: a) transmitting "stop if in SR mode"

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.31

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP b) not contained in the list of expected balises in SR mode c) transmitting "stop if in SH mode" d) not contained in the list of expected balises in SH mode" e) Intentionally deleted

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.1.8, PDF p.32

5.8.1.8 Further, the Override procedure allows a train in SR mode reaching the end of the SR distance to proceed (see also 4.4.11.1.4)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.2, PDF p.32

5.8.2 Selection of “Override”

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.2.1, PDF p.32

5.8.2.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall allow the driver to select “Override” only when: a) The train speed is under or equal to the speed limit for triggering the “override” function (national value) AND b) The current mode is Full Supervision, Limited Supervision, On Sight, Staff Responsible, Shunting, Unfitted, Post Trip, Stand By (in level 2/3 only) or SN (National System) AND c) Validated Train Data and Train running number are available (except when already in Shunting mode).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.2.2, PDF p.32

5.8.2.2 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.2.3, PDF p.32

5.8.2.3 The “Override” procedure shall be triggered when selected by the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3, PDF p.32

5.8.3 Once the “Override” procedure has been triggered

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.1, PDF p.32

5.8.3.1 The mode shall change as follows: a) If the current mode is Full Supervision, Limited Supervision, On Sight, Stand-By or Post Trip, the mode shall immediately switch to the Staff Responsible (SR) mode (if the mode is already SR it remains unchanged) b) If the current mode is Shunting the mode shall remain unchanged c) If the current mode is Unfitted (level 0 area) or SN (level NTC area) the mode shall only change to Staff Responsible when the level changes to 1,2 or 3 (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.1.1, PDF p.32

5.8.3.1.1 If the mode, when activating Override, is OS, LS or FS, the former EOA/LOA shall be retained. If the mode is SB or PT, the current position of the train front shall be considered as the former EOA/LOA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.1.2, PDF p.32

5.8.3.1.2 Note: This former EOA/LOA will be used as a Trip condition if the Override function is no longer active. Any further activation of the Override in SR mode has no effect on the former EOA/LOA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.32

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.1.3, PDF p.33

5.8.3.1.3 The former EOA/LOA shall be deleted if: a) the train reads the information “stop if in SR mode” from a balise group OR b) SR mode is left.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.2, PDF p.33

5.8.3.2 Note 1: In level 2, 3, if radio communication is available, the RBC is only informed that the Override has been triggered by means of the reported mode change (if there is any)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.3, PDF p.33

5.8.3.3 Note 2: In level 2,3, if the ERTMS/ETCS- onboard equipment is able to report the mode change to the RBC, the RBC may transmit limits for the distance to run in SR mode (overriding the national value), a list of balises to be passed in SR mode (refer to chapter 4, Staff Responsible mode)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.4, PDF p.33

5.8.3.4 Note 3: In level 2,3, the transition to SR mode triggered by selecting Override revokes all emergency stop orders previously received.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.5, PDF p.33

5.8.3.5 In SR mode the driver may modify the value of the SR mode speed limit and of the distance to run in SR mode (refer to chapter 4, Staff Responsible mode)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.6, PDF p.33

5.8.3.6 The train trip shall be inhibited (suppression of the transition to the Trip mode), and only in level 0, 1, 2, 3, the MRSP shall include the Override function related Speed Restriction (see 3.11.10) as long as the Override function is active.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.7, PDF p.33

5.8.3.7 The status “override active” shall be indicated to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.7.1, PDF p.33

5.8.3.7.1 Exception 1: In case the Override function has been activated by an STM (see SUBSET-035), the status “override active” shall not be indicated to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.7.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.7.2, PDF p.33

5.8.3.7.2 Exception 2: In case the Override function has been activated by selection of “Override” while being in level 0, 1, 2 or 3, the status “override active” shall stop to be indicated to the driver on executing a transition to level NTC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.8, PDF p.33

5.8.3.8 As long as the Override function is active, new SR distance information received from EUROLOOP shall be rejected.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.3.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.3.9, PDF p.33

5.8.3.9 When “Override” is selected and Override is already active, the supervision of the time and distance (see 5.8.4.1 a) and b)) for train trip suppression shall be re-started.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.4, PDF p.33

5.8.4 End of Override procedure

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.4.1, PDF p.33

5.8.4.1 The Override procedure shall end when at least one of the following conditions is fulfilled: a) The "max. time for train trip suppression when Override function is triggered" (national value) elapses after Override has been selected, OR b) The train has run more than the "distance for train trip suppression when Override function is triggered" (national value) after Override has been selected, OR

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.33

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP c) The former EOA/LOA has been passed with the min safe antenna position (calculated by subtracting distance between active EUROBALISE antenna and the front end of the train from the min safe front end position), OR d) The train passes a balise group giving “stop if in SR mode” or “stop if in SH mode” information, OR e) The train passes a balise group giving proceed information (i.e., MA with no signalling related speed restriction of value zero) f) In level 2,3, an MA is received from the RBC g) The train passes a balise group not in the list of expected balises in SR mode or the list of expected balises in SH mode h) The train overpasses the SR distance supervised before overriding with its estimated front end i) The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment switches to TR, LS, OS or SH mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.4.1.1, PDF p.34

5.8.4.1.1 Note: For modes UN and SN, only end conditions a) and b) are supervised.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.4.2, PDF p.34

5.8.4.2 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.8.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.8.4.3, PDF p.34

5.8.4.3 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.34

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.1, PDF p.35

5.9.1 General Requirements

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.1.1, PDF p.35

5.9.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall be in On Sight mode before the train reaches the beginning of the On Sight area or, at the latest, when the train reaches the beginning of the On Sight area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.1.2, PDF p.35

5.9.1.2 An acknowledgement for running in On Sight mode is requested from the driver. The conditions of the acknowledgement are specified below.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2, PDF p.35

5.9.2 On Sight is requested for current location (from modes different from Stand By and Post Trip)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2.1, PDF p.35

5.9.2.1 In a level 1 area, the beginning of the On Sight area can be the balise (group) that gives the Mode Profile. When the train passes the balise group and receives this information, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately switch to On Sight mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2.2, PDF p.35

5.9.2.2 In a level 2 or 3 area, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment can receive a mode profile giving an On Sight area which the train has already entered with its max safe front end. In this case, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately switch to On Sight mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2.3, PDF p.35

5.9.2.3 The driver must acknowledge the On Sight mode. A request of acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2.4, PDF p.35

5.9.2.4 If the driver has not acknowledged after the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A.3.1), the service brake command shall be triggered. The brake command is released when the driver acknowledges, except if brakes are also applied for another reason(s).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2.5, PDF p.35

5.9.2.5 Note: Once in On Sight mode, the speed supervision is such that the train speed cannot exceed the OS mode speed limit. If, when entering the On Sight mode, the train speed was higher than the OS mode speed limit (because a higher speed was allowed in Full Supervision mode, in Limited Supervision mode or in Staff Responsible mode) then a service/emergency brake command could be immediately triggered, independently of the acknowledgement of the driver, but because of the On Sight supervision (see Figure 4).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.35

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP Transition to OS mode triggers SB/EB command speed permitted speed (even if driver acknowledges in previous mode within 5s) Brake command revoked (conditions see SRS chapter 3, Dynamic Speed Monitoring) train speed permitted speed in OS mode Location of: OS request for location current location Figure 4: Train enters OS area with too high speed

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2.6, PDF p.36

5.9.2.6 Note: This sharp brake reaction can be avoided in Full Supervision or Limited Supervision mode by giving with the previous MA an EOA (or a LOA = OS mode speed limit) at the location of transition to On Sight mode. In Staff Responsible mode, lateral signals (if available) can also order the driver to decrease the train speed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.2.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.2.7, PDF p.36

5.9.2.7 If the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is already in OS mode when receiving the OS mode profile, no further acknowledgement shall be requested from the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3, PDF p.36

5.9.3 On Sight is requested for a further location

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.1, PDF p.36

5.9.3.1 The beginning of the On Sight area can be a location that the train has not reached yet. This occurs when: a) In a level 1 area, a balise group gives a Mode Profile with an On Sight area that is located at a further location. b) In a level 2 or 3 area, the RBC gives a Mode Profile with an On Sight area that is located at a further location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.2, PDF p.36

5.9.3.2 A request for acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver when the following conditions are fulfilled: a) The distance between the estimated front end of the train and the beginning of On Sight area is shorter than a value, contained in the mode profile. b) The speed is lower than the On Sight mode speed limit (national value, or value given in the mode profile). c) The current mode is not On Sight

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.3, PDF p.36

5.9.3.3 The conditions 5.9.3.2 a) and b) define the “rectangle of acknowledgement”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.4, PDF p.36

5.9.3.4 Once the acknowledgement request is displayed, it shall not be taken back if the train leaves the “rectangle of acknowledgement” (for example: because the train accelerates).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.36

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.5, PDF p.37

5.9.3.5 Until the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has switched to OS mode, the beginning of the On Sight area shall be temporarily considered as the EOA (instead of the EOA/LOA derived from the MA) and the SvL (with no release speed) shall be determined according to the mode profile either: a) as the SvL derived from the MA. In case the MA defines an LOA, the SvL shall be derived as if no LOA had been given. OR b) as the beginning of the On Sight area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.6, PDF p.37

5.9.3.6 When the driver acknowledges the On Sight mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately switch to the On Sight mode. braking curve in FS/LS mode acknowledge request is speed displayed to the driver driver acknowledges train speed Permitted Speed In OS mode location Beginning of the Acknowledgement On Sight area Area Transition to On Sight mode Figure 5: Transition from FS/LS to OS mode after driver acknowledgement

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.7, PDF p.37

5.9.3.7 If the max safe front end of the train reaches the beginning of the On Sight area according to the mode profile and the driver has not yet acknowledged, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch immediately to OS mode and a request for acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.3.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.3.8, PDF p.37

5.9.3.8 If, in this case, the driver does not acknowledge within the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A.3.1) after the change to OS mode, the service brake command shall be triggered. The command shall be released as soon as the driver acknowledges (unless the command was triggered also for other reasons).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.37

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.4, PDF p.38

5.9.4 On Sight from Unfitted or SN mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.4.1, PDF p.38

5.9.4.1 The mode profile with regards to an OS area is only evaluated in levels 1,2,3, although the mode profile may have been received in level 0 (Unfitted mode) or NTC (SN mode). A transition to On Sight mode can therefore earliest occur at a transition of level: from level 0 or NTC to level 1 or 2 or 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.4.2, PDF p.38

5.9.4.2 Requirements about the acknowledgement in section 5.9.2 shall apply.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.5, PDF p.38

5.9.5 On Sight from Stand By or Post Trip mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.5.1, PDF p.38

5.9.5.1 When performing a SoM or a Train Trip procedure and when the current level is 2 or 3, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment can receive a mode profile giving an On Sight area which the train has already entered with its max safe front end. In this case, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall first require an acknowledgement from the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.5.2, PDF p.38

5.9.5.2 When the driver acknowledges, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform the transition to On Sight mode.”

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6, PDF p.38

5.9.6 Exit of On Sight mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.1.1, PDF p.38

5.9.6.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall exit the On Sight mode when the min safe front end of the train passes the end of the On Sight area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.2, PDF p.38

5.9.6.2 First case: The On Sight area ends at the EOA/LOA of the current MA

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.2.1, PDF p.38

5.9.6.2.1 This occurs when the end of the On Sight area that is given by the Mode Profile has the same location as the EOA/LOA of the related MA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.2.2, PDF p.38

5.9.6.2.2 In this case, the train must receive a new Movement Authority to be able to exit the On Sight area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.2.3, PDF p.38

5.9.6.2.3 Note: In an On Sight area there is no guarantee for the RBC that the track in front of the supervised train is free. Therefore, if the next block section is free, the RBC has nevertheless to ensure that there is no train/vehicle between the train and the end of the On Sight area. This information  can be given to the RBC by the signalman or any other trackside means (outside scope of ERTMS/ETCS), or  can be inquired by the RBC by means of the following mechanism: the RBC sends a “track ahead free” request which the ERTMS/ ETCS on-board equipment displays to the driver. If the driver confirms that the track is free up to the end of the current section, the ERTMS/ ETCS on-board equipment will transmit this information to the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.38

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.2.4, PDF p.39

5.9.6.2.4 Note: Receiving the “track ahead free” information, the RBC may be able to transmit an MA from the current position of the train, e.g., for Full Supervision (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.3, PDF p.39

5.9.6.3 Second case: The On Sight area ends before the EOA/LOA of the current MA

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.3.1, PDF p.39

5.9.6.3.1 In this case, the current Movement Authority already allows the train to exit the On Sight area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.6.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.6.3.2, PDF p.39

5.9.6.3.2 When exiting the On Sight area, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment switches either to Full Supervision, to Limited Supervision or to Shunting mode (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.39

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.9.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.9.7, PDF p.40

5.9.7 Flowchart mode is FS, LS, OS, SR, SB, PT, UN, or SN A mode profile for OS area has been received and is used Max safe front Beginning of Transition to FS/LS mode further location inside OS area OS area (if not yet in FS/LS) Max safe front overpasses begin of OS area - Start of OS mode profile OS Mode SB,PT supervised as EoA - Waiting estimated front and speed in acknowledgement window FS,LS,SR,UN,SN - acknowledgement is Transition to requested to driver OS mode - Waiting for driver ackno Max safe front overpasses begin of OS area Driver acknowledges Transition to - acknowledgement is Driver acknowledges OS mode requested to driver within 5sec - Waiting for driver ackno 5 sec are elapsed & no ack by driver Service brake command until driver acknowledges Figure 6: Flowchart for “On-Sight”

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.40

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1, PDF p.41

5.10.1 General requirements

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.1, PDF p.41

5.10.1.1 Every level transition border to an area where operation in level 2, 3 or NTC is supported shall be announced to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment via balise group or via the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.2, PDF p.41

5.10.1.2 A level transition announcement to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall consist of an order to execute the level transition at a further location corresponding to the border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.3, PDF p.41

5.10.1.3 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment receives a level transition announcement, and if this announcement will result in a change of the on-board level, it shall immediately inform the driver about the announced level transition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.3.1, PDF p.41

5.10.1.3.1 Note: In a mixed level area the actual level of the on-board equipment may remain unchanged even though a level transition boundary is passed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.4, PDF p.41

5.10.1.4 At the level transition border a balise group shall be placed with an immediate level transition order or a conditional level transition order.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.4.1, PDF p.41

5.10.1.4.1 Note: Balise groups are read in all levels and level transition orders and conditional level transition orders from balises are accepted independent of the level of operation. Also sleeping units read balise groups. Announcement by RBC possible if communication session exists Announcement by Level balise group transition location Level X area Level Y area Figure 7: Transition from level X area to level Y area

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.5, PDF p.41

5.10.1.5 If the message from the border balise group is not received, the level transition shall still be executed when the estimated front end passes the location given in the announcement.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.6, PDF p.41

5.10.1.6 The on-board equipment shall manage only one level transition order at a time. Therefore a new level transition order shall replace a previously received order, i.e. if a new order to switch to a different level or to the same level but at a different location is received, before the action from the first order has been performed, only the last order shall be executed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.41

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.6.1, PDF p.42

5.10.1.6.1 In Shunting and Passive Shunting modes only one set of Level Transition Information shall be stored at a time. Therefore a set of Level Transition Information received shall replace any Level Transition Information already stored on-board.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.7, PDF p.42

5.10.1.7 As soon as the announcement of the level transition has been received, some data (mainly movement authority and track description data) from the transmission media of the new level shall be accepted, but shall not be used until the level transition is effective.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.7.1, PDF p.42

5.10.1.7.1 Note: for the exhaustive list of accepted/rejected information, please refer to SRS chapter 4.8.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.7.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.7.2, PDF p.42

5.10.1.7.2 Note: if only track description has been received from the new media without any movement authority, this track description still replaces the one previously received from the current media when the transition is performed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.8, PDF p.42

5.10.1.8 When the onboard has performed the level transition, further data (mainly movement authority and track description data) received from the transmission media of the level being left shall be rejected.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.8.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.8.1, PDF p.42

5.10.1.8.1 Note: for the exhaustive list of accepted/rejected information, please refer to SRS chapter 4.8.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.1.9

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.1.9, PDF p.42

5.10.1.9 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2, PDF p.42

5.10.2 Table of priority of trackside supported levels

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.1, PDF p.42

5.10.2.1 Any combination of ERTMS/ETCS levels 0, NTC, 1, 2, and 3 on a given area shall be possible.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.2, PDF p.42

5.10.2.2 The level transition announcement and the immediate or conditional level transition order at the border shall contain all the supported ERTMS/ETCS levels with a table of priority. Even if only one level is permitted this is considered as a table of priority.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.2.1, PDF p.42

5.10.2.2.1 Note: Level 0 is considered in the same way as the other levels. This means that, for example, when an area permits ERTMS/ETCS level 0, and is fitted with ERTMS/ETCS level 1 and 2, the track-side includes levels 0, 1 and 2 in a table of priority of supported levels in all level transition orders and conditional level transition orders applying to that area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.3, PDF p.42

5.10.2.3 The table of priority shall list all the supported levels from the highest priority level to the lowest one.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.3.1, PDF p.42

5.10.2.3.1 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.4, PDF p.42

5.10.2.4 When receiving the information about all ERTMS/ETCS levels that are supported by trackside, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall select from the table the level with the highest priority, which is available for use by the onboard equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.42

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.4.1, PDF p.43

5.10.2.4.1 The on-board equipment shall consider an ERTMS/ETCS level as “Available for use” as follows: a) Level 2 or 3: the level is configured on-board and at least one Mobile Terminal is available on-board, i.e. the ETCS onboard has detected at least one Mobile Terminal in working condition, independently whether it is registered to a network or not. b) Level NTC: the concerned National System is available on-board (if an STM is used, refer to SUBSET-035 for further details). c) Level 0 or 1: always.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.4.1.1, PDF p.43

5.10.2.4.1.1 Note regarding a) and b): how the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment checks the availability of the Mobile Terminals or of the National System (in case no STM is used) is an implementation issue.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.4.2, PDF p.43

5.10.2.4.2 Examples: The table of trackside supported levels gives 2, NTC X, 1, NTC Y. If level 1, 0 and NTC X are “Available for use”, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board will select NTC X level. If level 1, 0 and NTC Y are “Available for use”, it will select level 1. If level 2, 1 and 0 are “Available for use”, it will select level 2.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.5, PDF p.43

5.10.2.5 When the onboard has selected the level it will switch to, it shall carry out the level transition as if it has received a level transition order to this level only i.e. it shall ignore the requirements related to transitions to the other levels.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.6, PDF p.43

5.10.2.6 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall inform the driver about the selected level transition only.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.7, PDF p.43

5.10.2.7 If none of the ordered level(s) is available for use by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment, it shall nevertheless make the transition, to the ordered level with the lowest priority.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.7.1, PDF p.43

5.10.2.7.1 Justification: The On-board equipment will then indicate the trackside level to the driver to allow him to select the correct procedures for degraded situations.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.2.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.2.8, PDF p.43

5.10.2.8 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall store the table of priority of trackside supported ERTMS/ETCS levels.

5.10.2.9 Intentionally deleted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3, PDF p.43

5.10.3 Specific Additional Requirements

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.1, PDF p.43

5.10.3.1 Transition from Level 1 to Level 2/3 area

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.1.1, PDF p.43

5.10.3.1.1 An order to connect to the RBC with a given id and telephone number shall be given via balise group in rear of the border location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.43

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.1.2, PDF p.44

5.10.3.1.2 For the train to be able to enter the new area, the old area must possess information about at least the first section of the new area. The information shall be transmitted to the train either: a) as an MA and track description information into the new area, or b) as a target speed at the border location i.e. as an LOA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.1.3, PDF p.44

5.10.3.1.3 When the ERTMS/ETCS communication session is open, Train Data shall be sent to the RBC (which acknowledges the data) unless the onboard equipment is in SL or NL mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.1.4, PDF p.44

5.10.3.1.4 If no Level 2/3 MA and track description has been received when entering the new area, the train shall still be supervised according to the level 1 MA previously received.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.1.5, PDF p.44

5.10.3.1.5 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has switched to the new level, it shall report the new on-board level, including a position report.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.1.6, PDF p.44

5.10.3.1.6 If an order to connect to an RBC has been received and the train will not enter the announced RBC area, an order to terminate the session shall be sent either from balises or from the RBC for any route not leading to the RBC area. This is the case both if the train turns back and if the train continues in the same direction, but on another route.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.2, PDF p.44

5.10.3.2 Transition from Level 0 (Unfitted) to Level 2/3 area

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.2.1, PDF p.44

5.10.3.2.1 An order to connect to the RBC with a given id and telephone number shall be given via balise group in rear of the border location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.2.2, PDF p.44

5.10.3.2.2 When the ERTMS/ETCS communication session is open, Train Data shall be sent to the RBC (which acknowledges the data) unless the onboard equipment is in SL or NL mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.2.3, PDF p.44

5.10.3.2.3 A level 2/3 MA and track description information shall be received from the RBC before the level transition border. If not, the train will be tripped at passage of the border, i.e. after switching to level 2 or 3, movement is not allowed without a movement authority (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.2.4, PDF p.44

5.10.3.2.4 The driver is responsible for entering the level 2/3 area at a speed not exceeding the speed limits of the unequipped line.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.2.5, PDF p.44

5.10.3.2.5 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has switched to the new level, it shall report the new on-board level, including a position report.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.2.6, PDF p.44

5.10.3.2.6 If an order to connect to an RBC has been received and the train will not enter the announced RBC area, an order to terminate the session shall be sent either from balises or from the RBC for any route not leading to the RBC area. This is the case both if the train turns back and if the train continues in the same direction, but on another route.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.44

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.3, PDF p.45

5.10.3.3 Transition from Level 2/3 to Level 1 area

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.3.1, PDF p.45

5.10.3.3.1 For the train to be able to enter the new area, the old area must possess information about at least the first section of the new area. The information shall be transmitted to the train either a) as an MA and track description information into the new area, or b) as a target speed at the border location i.e. as an LOA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.3.2, PDF p.45

5.10.3.3.2 If no Level 1 MA and track description has been received when entering the new area, the train shall still be supervised according to the level 2/3 MA previously received from the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.3.3, PDF p.45

5.10.3.3.3 When the train has passed the level transition border with its min safe rear end, i.e. when the whole train has left the level 2/3 area, the onboard equipment of the leading engine shall send a position report to the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.3.4, PDF p.45

5.10.3.3.4 After receiving this exit position report, the RBC can order the train to terminate the session (leading and non-leading engines).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.3.5, PDF p.45

5.10.3.3.5 In case the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has reported that the train has passed with its min safe rear end the level transition border and no order to terminate the session is received within a fixed waiting time (see Appendix A.3.1) from the time the position report was sent, it shall repeatedly send a position report with the fixed waiting time after each repetition, until the order to terminate the session is received, or the defined number of repetitions (see Appendix A.3.1) has been reached. If no reply is received within the fixed waiting time after the last repetition, the ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment shall terminate the communication session.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.4, PDF p.45

5.10.3.4 Transition from Level 0 (Unfitted) to Level 1 area

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.4.1, PDF p.45

5.10.3.4.1 A level 1 MA and track description information shall be received before or at the level transition border. If not, when the level transition is performed, the train will be tripped, i.e. after switching to level 1, movement is not allowed without a movement authority (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.4.2, PDF p.45

5.10.3.4.2 The driver is responsible for entering the level 1 area at a speed not exceeding the speed limits of the unequipped line.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.5, PDF p.45

5.10.3.5.1 For the train to be able to enter the new area, the old area must possess information about at least the first section of the new area. The information shall be transmitted to the train either a) as an MA and track description information into the new area, or b) as a target speed at the border location i.e. as an LOA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.14

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.14, PDF p.49

5.10.3.14 Conditional level transition order

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.14.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.14.1, PDF p.49

5.10.3.14.1 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment accepts a conditional level transition order the onboard shall check whether the current level is contained in the priority list of the conditional level transition order.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.14.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.14.2, PDF p.49

5.10.3.14.2 If the current level is contained in the priority list of the conditional level transition order, the onboard shall not change the level.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.14.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.14.3, PDF p.49

5.10.3.14.3 If the current level is not contained in the priority list of the conditional level transition order, the onboard shall evaluate the conditional level transition order in the same way as an immediate level transition order (see section 5.10.2).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.14.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.14.4, PDF p.49

5.10.3.14.4 In the same way as for a level transition order, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall store the table of ERTMS/ETCS levels supported by trackside.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.14.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.14.5, PDF p.49

5.10.3.14.5 Note: The conditional level transition order allows to check, whether a train operates in a permitted level e.g. following a start of mission after a cold movement. The level of a train driving in a permitted level will not be changed, regardless of the priority of the current level operated by the train.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.15

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.15, PDF p.49

5.10.3.15 Transition initiated by driver

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.15.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.15.1, PDF p.49

5.10.3.15.1 In addition to the level transitions ordered by trackside, it is also possible, at standstill, for the driver to change the ERTMS/ETCS level (refer to section 3.18.4.2).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.15.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.15.2, PDF p.49

5.10.3.15.2 If the driver changes the level to 2 or 3, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall establish a communication session with the RBC: a) immediately if at least one Mobile Terminal is registered to a Radio Network and a valid RBC ID/ phone number is available, OR b) once the driver has selected the Radio data (by the same means as for Start of Mission), if either no Mobile Terminal is registered to a Radio Network or no valid RBC ID/phone number is available.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.15.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.15.2.1, PDF p.49

5.10.3.15.2.1 Note regarding b): If the level transition leads to TR mode, the request for RBC contact information is only displayed once the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is in PT mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.15.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.15.3, PDF p.49

5.10.3.15.3 If the driver changes the level from 2 or 3 to any other, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall report the new level to the RBC if a communication session is established. When receiving the level change report, the RBC shall order the communication session to be terminated.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.3.15.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.3.15.4, PDF p.49

5.10.3.15.4 In case the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has reported having changed from level 2/3 to any other and no order to terminate the session is received within a fixed

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.49

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP waiting time (see Appendix A.3.1) from the time the position report was sent, it shall repeatedly send a position report with the fixed waiting time after each repetition, until the order to terminate the session is received, or the defined number of repetitions (see Appendix A.3.1) has been reached. If no reply is received within the fixed waiting time after the last repetition, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall terminate the communication session.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.4, PDF p.50

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.4.1, PDF p.50

5.10.4.1 If defined so for the level transition (see table below), the driver shall be requested to acknowledge the transition a) when the max safe front end of the train has passed a trackside defined location in rear of the level transition border b) upon receipt of the order to switch to the new level immediately

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.4.1.1, PDF p.50

5.10.4.1.1 Exception: An ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment in NL mode shall not require an acknowledgement from the driver.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.4.1.2, PDF p.50

5.10.4.1.2 Exception to 5.10.4.1.a): in SB mode, the driver shall be requested to acknowledge the level transition only when the level changes.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.10.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.4.2, PDF p.50

5.10.4.2 If the driver has not yet acknowledged within the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A.3.1) after the level transition, a service brake command shall be initiated.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.10.4.3, PDF p.50

5.10.4.3 The service brake command shall then be released when the driver acknowledges the level transition.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11, PDF p.51

5.11 Procedure Train Trip

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.1.1, PDF p.51

5.11.1.1 A train can be tripped for various reasons: refer to SRS chapter 4, mode transition table.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.2, PDF p.51

5.11.2 Table of requirements for “Train Trip” procedure

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.2.1, PDF p.51

5.11.2.1 The ID numbers in the table are used for the representation of the procedure in form of a flowchart in section 5.11.3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.2.2, PDF p.51

5.11.2.2 Procedure ID # Requirements S010 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is in one of the following modes: FS, LS, OS, SR, SB, SH, SN or UN When an event occurs, which leads to train trip reaction (E015 – refer to chapter 4, transitions between modes), the process shall go to A025. A025 The mode shall change to TR. The process shall go to D020. D020 If the level is 1, the process shall go to A035. If the level is 2/3, the process shall go to A030. If the level is 0/NTC, the process shall go to S050. A030 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall report the mode change to the RBC The process shall go to A035. A035 All current MA and track description data (if any), except track conditions, shall be deleted and new ones shall not be accepted The process shall go to S050. S050 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment awaits standstill. While braking a border to a level 0 or NTC area may be passed. When the train has come to standstill (E055), the process shall go to S060. S060 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall display the "Request for driver acknowledgement to Train Trip" to the driver. When the driver acknowledges the Train Trip (E065), the process shall go to D080.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.51

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP ID # Requirements D80 If the level is 1, 2 or 3 the process shall go to A105. If the level is 0 or NTC, the process shall go to D085 A105 The mode shall change to PT and the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment revokes the emergency brake command. For the supervision provided by the PT mode refer to SRS chapter 4. The process shall go to D110. D085 If no valid Train Data is stored on-board, the process shall go to A140 If valid Train Data is stored on-board, the process shall go to D090 A140 The mode shall change to SH and the process shall END. D090 If the level is 0, the process shall go to A145. If the level is NTC, the process shall go to A150. A145 The mode shall change to UN and the process shall END. A150 The mode shall change to SN and the process shall END. D110 If the level is 1, the process shall go to S140. If the level is 2 or 3, the process shall go to A115. A115 The mode change to PT shall be reported to the RBC which shall acknowledge the mode report (Recognition of exit from TR). The process shall go to S120. S120 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment waits for the RBC to acknowledge the transition to PT. When the acknowledgement is received from the RBC (E125), the process shall go to D130. Note: See 5.11.4 for degraded situation (no response received). D130 If there is at least one pending emergency stop, the process shall go to S130. If there are no pending emergency stops the process shall go to S140. S130 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment waits for the RBC to revoke ALL pending emergency stops. When all emergency stops are revoked (E135) the process shall go to S140.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.52

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP ID # Requirements S140 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall offer the possibility to the driver to select "start" (only if train data has been previously entered), or to select SH a) If the driver selects "start" and the level is 1 (E150), the process shall go to S160 b) If the driver selects "start" and the level is 2 or 3 (E155), the process shall go to S150 c) If the driver selects SH (E145), the process shall continue in the same ways as the procedure “Shunting initiated by the driver”. If the SH request is refused by the RBC (E165) the process shall return to S140. S150 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall send an MA request to the RBC and wait. a) If an SR authorisation is received from RBC (E26), the process shall go to S160 b) If an MA allowing OS/LS/SH is received from RBC (E175), the process shall go to S170 c) If an MA allowing FS is received from RBC (E170), the mode shall change to FS (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes: transition from PT to FS) and the process shall END. S160 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall request an acknowledgement from the driver for running in SR mode. When the driver acknowledges (E180), the mode shall change to SR (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes: transition from PT to SR) and the process shall END. S170 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall request an acknowledgement from the driver for running in OS/LS/SH mode. When the driver acknowledges (E185), the mode shall change to OS/LS/SH (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes: transition from PT to OS/LS/SH) and the process shall END.
