SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.4, PDF p.56

5.11.4 Degraded Situations

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.4.1, PDF p.56

5.11.4.1 ERTMS/ETCS level 2 or 3: no acknowledge for PT mode is received from the RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.4.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.4.1.1, PDF p.56

5.11.4.1.1 In case a communication session is established and no reply is received from the RBC within a fixed waiting time (see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data) after reporting the mode change, the report shall be repeated with the fixed waiting time after each repetition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.4.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.4.1.2, PDF p.56

5.11.4.1.2 After a defined number of repetitions(see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data) and if no reply is received within the fixed waiting time from the last sending of the mode change report, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall terminate the communication session.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.11.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.11.4.2, PDF p.56

5.11.4.2 Nominally, accidental loss of an already open session (that can occur at any step) has not been taken into account for the design of the flowchart. However, should such a fault occur in any step while ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is in level 2/3 and in PT mode, the driver shall have the possibility to select "Override" if the conditions defined in 5.8.2.1 are fulfilled and the process shall go to the procedure "Override".

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.56

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12, PDF p.57

5.12 Change of Train Orientation

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.1.1, PDF p.57

5.12.1.1 The scope of this procedure is the supervision of a train where the driver controls the train from the cab in the front of the train with the direction controller in FORWARD position.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.1.2, PDF p.57

5.12.1.2 This implies that when the driver has to change the orientation of the train, he has to change the driving cab.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.1.3, PDF p.57

5.12.1.3 The scope of this procedure is NOT shunting movements, during which the driver changes the running direction of the train without leaving the cab, by changing the position of the direction controller from FORWARD to REVERSE.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.1.4, PDF p.57

5.12.1.4 The scope of this procedure is NOT the backwards movement that is allowed in Post Trip or in Reversing mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.2, PDF p.57

5.12.2 The driver uses the same engine (a mission is ongoing)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.2.1, PDF p.57

5.12.2.1 The situation is the following: The driver closes the desk A and leaves the cab A of the leading engine of the train, to go to cab B and open desk B of this same engine.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.2.2, PDF p.57

5.12.2.2 Desk A and desk B are connected to the same ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.2.3, PDF p.57

5.12.2.3 When the driver closes the desk A, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment immediately goes to Stand-By mode, which is considered as an end of mission (see “End of Mission” procedure).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.2.4, PDF p.57

5.12.2.4 When the driver opens the desk B, the “Start of Mission” procedure is triggered.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.2.5, PDF p.57

5.12.2.5 When the driver closes a desk and opens the other one of the same engine, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall be able to calculate the new train position data (train front position, train orientation), by use of the previous data.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3, PDF p.57

5.12.3 The driver leaves the engine to go to another one

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.1, PDF p.57

5.12.3.1 The described situation is the following: The train has two engines (engine A and engine B). The engine A is the leading engine. The engine B is a slave engine. Each engine has its own ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment. a) If engine B is remote controlled, its ETCS on-board equipment is in Sleeping mode. Note: The mode is entered when on-board equipment detects the presence of the "remote control" signal.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.57

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP b) If the slave engine is not remote controlled (Tandem operation) by the leading engine but there is a driver who controls the engine, then the on-board equipment is in Non leading mode. c) If the engine B is not remote controlled (Tandem Shunting operation) by the leading engine and there is no driver who controls the engine, then the on-board equipment is in Passive Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.2, PDF p.58

5.12.3.2 Assumption: The train configuration does not change. a) When changing the train orientation, the leading engine A will become the slave engine, and the slave engine B will become the leading engine. b) If before the change of train orientation engine B was in SL, afterwards engine A will be in SL mode; If before the change of train orientation engine B was in NL, afterwards engine A will be in NL mode; If before the change of train orientation engine B was in PS, afterwards engine A will be in PS mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.3, PDF p.58

5.12.3.3 Case "Engine B was in SL mode"

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.3.1, PDF p.58

5.12.3.3.1 The driver of engine A closes the desk, then the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of engine A switches to Stand-By mode. If the train has a mission, this is a end of mission (see “End of Mission” procedure)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.3.2, PDF p.58

5.12.3.3.2 As soon as the remote control signal disappears, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of engine B switches to Stand-By mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.3.3, PDF p.58

5.12.3.3.3 Level 2,3: The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of engine B opens a communication session (if possible) and reports the mode change to the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.3.4, PDF p.58

5.12.3.3.4 When the driver opens a desk of engine B he triggers the "Start of Mission" procedure.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.4, PDF p.58

5.12.3.4 Case "Engine B was in NL mode"

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.4.1, PDF p.58

5.12.3.4.1 The driver of engine A selects "Non Leading". The ERTMS/ETCS equipment switches to Non Leading mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.4.2, PDF p.58

5.12.3.4.2 Once the non leading input signal is not received any more, the ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment of engine B will switch to Stand-By mode (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes and chapter 5, “End of Mission” procedure).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.4.3, PDF p.58

5.12.3.4.3 Because the desk is open, when the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment enters Stand- By mode, the “Start of Mission” procedure is triggered.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.5, PDF p.58

5.12.3.5 Case "Engine B was in PS mode"

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.5.1, PDF p.58

5.12.3.5.1 The driver of engine A selects "Continue Shunting on desk closure". The ERTMS/ETCS equipment switches to Passive Shunting mode once the driver closes the desk of engine A.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.58

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.3.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.3.5.2, PDF p.59

5.12.3.5.2 The driver opens a desk in engine B, and ERTMS/ETCS equipment switches to Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.4, PDF p.59

5.12.4 The driver uses the same engine (a Shunting movement is ongoing)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.4.1, PDF p.59

5.12.4.1 The situation is the following: while the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is in Shunting mode, the driver closes the desk A and leaves the cab A of the Shunting engine, to go to cab B and open desk B of this same engine.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.4.2, PDF p.59

5.12.4.2 Desk A and desk B are connected to the same ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.4.2.1, PDF p.59

5.12.4.2.1 Before closing the desk A, the driver enables the function “Continue Shunting on desk closure”. When the driver closes the desk A, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately go to Passive Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.4.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.4.2.2, PDF p.59

5.12.4.2.2 When the driver opens the desk B, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately switch back to Shunting mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.12.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.12.4.3, PDF p.59

5.12.4.3 When the driver closes a desk and opens the other one of the same engine, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall be able to calculate the new train position data (train front position, train orientation), by use of the previous data.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.59

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.1, PDF p.60

5.13.1.1 This procedure is intended to allow the fast reversal of movement of a train, to run away from a danger up to a “safe” location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.2, PDF p.60

5.13.1.2 The area where initiation of reversing will be possible is announced to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment by trackside (refer to 3.15.4.2 for details).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.3, PDF p.60

5.13.1.3 While the train is at standstill inside the reversing permitted area, the driver shall be informed that reversing is possible

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.4, PDF p.60

5.13.1.4 If the ERTMS/ETCS onboard detects the driver’s intention to reverse (e.g. from a direction controller in reverse position), the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall ask the driver to acknowledge transition to RV mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.5, PDF p.60

5.13.1.5 If the driver acknowledges, the on-board equipment shall switch to RV mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.6, PDF p.60

5.13.1.6 Once in RV mode, it shall be possible for the trackside to send a new permitted distance to run and a new maximum speed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.7, PDF p.60

5.13.1.7 Once in RV mode, it shall also be possible for the trackside to send, together with the new permitted distance to run and the maximum speed, a new reference location for the new permitted distance to run.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.13.1.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.13.1.8, PDF p.60

5.13.1.8 Note: this new reference location is the end of a new reversing area given by trackside that the onboard will use only for the purpose of distance referencing.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.60

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.1.1, PDF p.61

5.14.1.1 Definition for splitting: The “train to be split” is the train at standstill, waiting for being split. The “front train after splitting” refers to the front part of the train before splitting, the “new train after splitting”, refers to the other part.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.1.2, PDF p.61

5.14.1.2 Definitions for joining: The “train to be joined” is the train at standstill, waiting for being joined. The “joining train” is the train performing the joining operation.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.2, PDF p.61

5.14.2 Procedure “Splitting”

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.2.1, PDF p.61

5.14.2.1 Step 1 - The electrical and mechanical links between the two trains must be removed (this is a national operational procedure, out of the scope of the SRS).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.2.1.1, PDF p.61

5.14.2.1.1 Note: If splitting requires moving the two train parts apart from each other for a small distance, this can be done even in SB mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.2.2, PDF p.61

5.14.2.2 Step 2a - If the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment which was supervising the train before splitting has not performed an end of mission for splitting, the driver must modify the Train Data such that it fits with the new train composition after splitting. For level 2 or 3, the new train data is sent to the RBC (see SRS chapter 3 – Data Entry / Modification Process)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.2.3, PDF p.61

5.14.2.3 Step 2b - If an ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of the "new train after splitting" was in SL mode before, it will switch to SB mode once the remote control signal is not received any more (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes). For Level 2 or 3: The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment opens a communication session (if possible) and reports the mode change to the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.2.4, PDF p.61

5.14.2.4 Step 2c - If an ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment of the "new train after splitting" was in NL mode before, it will switch to SB mode once the non leading input signal is not received any more (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes and chapter 5, “end of mission” procedure).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.2.5, PDF p.61

5.14.2.5 The driver can then start a new mission with this “new train after splitting” (refer to the “Start of Mission” procedure). In all cases, to start a mission is not the only possibility. Shunting movements, or not moving the new train at all, are also possible.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.3, PDF p.61

5.14.3 Procedure “Joining”

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.3.1, PDF p.61

5.14.3.1 Step 1 - The “joining train” must approach the “train to be joined”. This can be performed in SR, OS or SH mode (depending on the information available, and on the national procedure for joining).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.61

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.3.2, PDF p.62

5.14.3.2 Step 2 - The electrical and mechanical links between the two trains must be closed (vehicle dependent, outside the scope of the ETCS).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.3.3, PDF p.62

5.14.3.3 Step 3a - If a former leading ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment remains leading and there was no end of mission, the driver must modify the Train Data such that it fits with the new train composition. For level 2 or 3, the new train data is sent to the RBC (see SRS chapter 3 – Data Entry / Modification Process)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.3.4, PDF p.62

5.14.3.4 Step 3b - If a former leading ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is to become slave equipment in SL mode, when closing the desk, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment will switch to SB mode (see SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes) and the end of mission procedure is executed (see “End of Mission” procedure). Transition to SL mode is from SB mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.3.5, PDF p.62

5.14.3.5 Step 3c - If a former leading ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is to become slave equipment in NL mode, the driver selects NL mode (see SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.14.3.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.14.3.6, PDF p.62

5.14.3.6 For further steps after joining refer to procedures “Start of Mission” and “Change of Train Orientation”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.62

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.1, PDF p.63

5.15.1.1 Every RBC/RBC handover shall be announced to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment via a balise group or via the RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.2, PDF p.63

5.15.1.2 The handover announcement (i.e. RBC transition order) to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall consist of an order to contact the Accepting RBC (see 3.5.3.5.3) and to execute the handover at a further location corresponding to the border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.2.1, PDF p.63

5.15.1.2.1 In case of RBC/RBC handover including Radio Network change, ERTMS/ETCS trackside is responsible for the sequence of orders to register to the new Radio Network and to contact the "Accepting" RBC, according to the Radio Network’s configuration.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.2.2, PDF p.63

5.15.1.2.2 In the following sections, "first" Mobile Terminal refers to the one used for communication session with “Handing Over” RBC and "second" Mobile Terminal to the one used for communication session with “Accepting” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.2.3, PDF p.63

5.15.1.2.3 Note: In the following sections, Radio Networks are supposed to be overlapped.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.3, PDF p.63

5.15.1.3 At the RBC/RBC border a balise group with an order to execute the handover immediately shall be placed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.3.1, PDF p.63

5.15.1.3.1 Note: Balise groups are read in all levels and orders from balise groups are accepted independent of the level of operation. Also sleeping units read balise groups.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.4, PDF p.63

5.15.1.4 If the message from the border balise group is not (yet) received, the handover shall still be executed when the train with its max safe front end passes the border location according to the announcement information.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.1.5, PDF p.63

5.15.1.5 The on-board equipment shall manage only one RBC/RBC transition at a time, therefore a new transition order shall replace a previously received order.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.1.1, PDF p.63

5.15.2.1.1 In the normal operation, the main functional steps needed for running from one RBC area to another one are the following: a) Pre-announcement of the transition by the “Handing Over” RBC; b) Registration to the new Radio Network of second Mobile Terminal (optional) & Establishment of the radio communication session with the “Accepting” RBC; c) Generation of movement authorities including the border;

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.63

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP d) Announcement of the RBC transition e) Transfer of train supervision to the “Accepting” RBC; f) Termination of the session with “Handing Over” RBC. g) Registration to the new Radio Network of first Mobile Terminal (optional)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2 Step by step description

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.1, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.1 Pre-announcement

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.1.1, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.1.1 When the “Handing Over” RBC generates a movement authority which reaches the border to another RBC area, it initiates the processes associated to the transition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.1.2, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.1.2 The “Handing Over” RBC informs the “Accepting” RBC about the RBC/RBC handover.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.2, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.2 Registration to the new Radio Network of second Mobile Terminal (optional) & Establishment of the radio communication session with “Accepting” RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.2.1, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.2.1 A radio communication session with the Accepting RBC is opened by the on-board equipment based on the RBC transition order received from the “Handing Over” RBC or from balise group (refer to chapter 3, section "management of radio communication").

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.2.2, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.2.2 In case of RBC/RBC handover including Radio Network change, the registration to the new radio network of the second Mobile Terminal is completed before the RBC transition order is transmitted to the on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.3, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.3 Generation of MAs including the border

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.3.1, PDF p.64

5.15.2.2.3.1 The “Handing Over” RBC is responsible for establishing the movement authority based on: a) Information from the trackside equipment and interlocking of its own area (for the part of route related information up to the border), b) Information from the “Accepting RBC” for the part of route related information in advance of the border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.64

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP MA sent by “Handing Over” RBC Route related information from Route related information from “Handing Over” RBC “Accepting” RBC Balise group at LRBG MA the border request route information “Handing “Accepting” Over” RBC RBC route information Figure 9: RBC to RBC transition: MA generation.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.3.2, PDF p.65

5.15.2.2.3.2 When it is required to send a movement authority to the train, the “Handing Over” RBC will request from the “Accepting” RBC information needed for extending the MA in advance of the border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.4.1, PDF p.65

5.15.2.2.4.1 When the train reaches the border with its max safe front end, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment sends a position report both to the “Handing Over” RBC and to the “Accepting” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.4.2, PDF p.65

5.15.2.2.4.2 The “Handing Over” RBC forwards the announcement information to the “Accepting” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.4.2.1, PDF p.65

5.15.2.2.4.2.1 Note: The forwarding of the announcement information is executed because the “Handing Over” RBC has no knowledge if the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is in a degraded situation or not i.e. whether it can handle one or two communication sessions.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.5, PDF p.65

5.15.2.2.5 Transfer of train supervision to “Accepting” RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.5.1, PDF p.65

5.15.2.2.5.1 As soon as the on-board has sent to the “Accepting” RBC the position report, it considers to be supervised by the “Accepting” RBC i.e. it uses information received from the “Accepting” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.5.2, PDF p.65

5.15.2.2.5.2 When the “Accepting” RBC receives a position report from the on-board and detects that the max safe front end has passed the border, it takes over the responsibility and informs the “Handing Over” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.65

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.6, PDF p.66

5.15.2.2.6 Termination of the session with “Handing Over” RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.6.1, PDF p.66

5.15.2.2.6.1 When the min safe rear end of the train passes the location of the border, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment sends a position report to the “Handing Over” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.6.2, PDF p.66

5.15.2.2.6.2 When this position report is received by the ”Handing Over” RBC, it sends an order to terminate the session to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.7, PDF p.66

5.15.2.2.7 Registration to the new Radio Network of first Mobile Terminal (optional)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.2.2.7.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.2.2.7.1, PDF p.66

5.15.2.2.7.1 In case of RBC/RBC handover including Radio Network change, the registration to the new Radio Network of the first Mobile Terminal is initiated by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment as soon as the communication session with the "Handing Over" RBC has been terminated and the safe radio connection has been released.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3, PDF p.66

5.15.3 Degraded situation: Only one communication session can be handled

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.1.1, PDF p.66

5.15.3.1.1 In this case, the main functional steps needed for running from one RBC area to another one are the following: a) Pre-announcement of the transition by the “Handing Over” RBC; b) Generation of movement authorities including the border; c) Announcement of the RBC transition d) Termination of the session with “Handing Over” RBC; e) Registration to the new Radio Network of the Mobile Terminal (optional) & Establishment of the radio communication session with the “Accepting” RBC; f) Transfer of train supervision to the “Accepting” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2, PDF p.66

5.15.3.2 Step by step description

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.1, PDF p.66

5.15.3.2.1 Pre-announcement

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.1.1, PDF p.66

5.15.3.2.1.1 When the “Handing over” RBC generates a movement authority which reaches the border to another RBC area, it initiates the processes associated to the transition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.1.2, PDF p.66

5.15.3.2.1.2 The “Handing Over” RBC informs the “Accepting” RBC about the RBC/RBC transition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.2, PDF p.66

5.15.3.2.2 Generation of MAs including the border

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.2.1, PDF p.66

5.15.3.2.2.1 The “Handing Over” RBC is responsible for establishing the movement authority based on (see Figure 9) a) Information from the trackside equipment and interlocking of its own area (for the part of route related information up to the border),

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.66

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP b) Information from the “Accepting RBC” for the part of route related information in advance of the border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.2.2, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.2.2 When it is required to send a movement authority to the train, the "Handing Over" RBC will request from the "Accepting RBC" information needed for extending the MA in advance of the border.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.3.1, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.3.1 When the train with its max safe front end reaches the border, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment sends a position report to the “Handing Over” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.3.2, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.3.2 The “Handing Over” RBC forwards the announcement information to the “Accepting” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.4, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.4 Termination of the session with “Handing Over” RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.4.1, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.4.1 As requested by the RBC transition order, when the min safe rear end of the train passes the location of the border, the on-board equipment sends a position report to the “Handing Over” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.4.2, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.4.2 When this position report is received by the “Handing Over” RBC, it sends an order to terminate the session to the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.5, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.5 Registration to the new Radio Network of the Mobile Terminal (optional) & Establishment of the radio communication session with “Accepting” RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.5.1, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.5.1 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment receives the session termination order from the “Handing Over” RBC, it terminates the session with the “Handing over” RBC and opens a session with the “Accepting” RBC (refer to chapter 3, management of radio communication).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.5.2, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.5.2 In case of RBC/RBC handover including Radio Network change: as soon as the session with the "Handing Over" RBC is terminated, the registration to the new Radio Network of the Mobile Terminal is enforced by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment prior to the opening of a session with the “Accepting” RBC (refer to chapter 3, management of radio communication).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.6, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.6 Transfer of train supervision to “Accepting” RBC

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.6.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.6.1, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.6.1 When the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has established a communication session with the “Accepting” RBC and sent to the “Accepting” RBC a position report, it considers to be supervised by the “Accepting” RBC, i.e. it accepts only information received from the “Accepting” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.3.2.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.3.2.6.2, PDF p.67

5.15.3.2.6.2 When the “Accepting” RBC receives a position report from the on-board and detects that the max safe front end has passed the border, it takes over the responsibility and informs the “Handing Over” RBC.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.67

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.4, PDF p.68

5.15.4 Other degraded Situations

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.4.1, PDF p.68

5.15.4.1 Note: If the “Handing Over” RBC is not able to extend the MA into the area of the “Accepting RBC”, the driver may select "override", or manually change the level to move the train into the area of the “Accepting RBC”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.4.2, PDF p.68

5.15.4.2 Note: If the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment cannot open a session with the “Accepting RBC”, the train is stopped at the latest when it has reached the EOA given by the “Handing Over” RBC. For passing the EOA the driver may select "override", or manually change the level.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.4.3, PDF p.68

5.15.4.3 If the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is not able to terminate the session with the “Handing Over” RBC: In case a communication session is established and no request to terminate the session is received from the “Handing Over” RBC within a fixed waiting time (see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data) after sending the position report (see 5.15.2.2.6), the position report shall be repeated with the fixed waiting time after each repetition.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.15.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.15.4.4, PDF p.68

5.15.4.4 After a defined number of repetitions (see appendix to chapter 3, List of Fixed Value Data), and if no reply is received within the fixed waiting time from the last sending of the position report, the ERTMS/ETCS onboard equipment shall terminate the communication session.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16, PDF p.68

5.16 Procedure passing a non protected Level Crossing

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.1, PDF p.68

5.16.1 General Requirements

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.1.1, PDF p.68

5.16.1.1 In case the LX is not protected, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment (in FS, LS or OS mode) shall temporarily supervise the LX start location as both the EOA and SvL (instead of the EOA/LOA and the SvL (if any) derived from the MA), with no release speed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.1.2, PDF p.68

5.16.1.2 The supervision of the LX start location as both the EOA and SvL shall be substituted by the inclusion of the LX speed restriction in the MRSP under conditions depending on whether stopping in rear of the LX start location is required or not. The conditions of this substitution are specified in 5.16.2 or 5.16.3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.1.3, PDF p.68

5.16.1.3 The start location of the LX speed restriction depends on the substitution conditions, which are specified in 5.16.2 or 5.16.3. The end location of the LX speed restriction shall be the LX end location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.1.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.1.4, PDF p.68

5.16.1.4 When approaching a non protected LX, the on-board equipment shall inform the driver about the status of the LX, as soon as: a) either the EOA or the SvL related to the LX start location becomes the Most Relevant Displayed Target (see 3.13.10.4.2), or

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.68

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP b) the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment substitutes the supervision of the LX start location as both the EOA and SvL by the inclusion of the LX speed restriction in the MRSP.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.1.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.1.5, PDF p.69

5.16.1.5 Indication given to the driver shall remain displayed until one of the following conditions is met: a) information “LX is protected” is received on-board; b) train has passed the LX end location with its min safe front end.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.2, PDF p.69

5.16.2 Stopping in rear of non protected LX is required

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.2.1, PDF p.69

5.16.2.1 Once the train has stopped with its estimated front end inside the stopping area, given by trackside, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall no longer supervise the LX start location as both the EOA and SvL (i.e. the EOA/LOA and the SvL (if any) derived from the MA shall be again supervised) and shall immediately include the LX speed restriction in the MRSP, starting from the estimated train front end. braking curve in FS/LS/OS mode speed Train at standstill train speed LX Speed train front end location LX start location Stopping Area LX speed is supervised Figure 10: Approaching a non protected LX with stopping required

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.3, PDF p.69

5.16.3 Stopping in rear of non protected LX is not required

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.3.1, PDF p.69

5.16.3.1 In case stopping in rear of the non protected LX is not required, the LX start location shall be supervised as both the EOA and SvL until the train reaches the location of the braking to target Permitted speed supervision limit calculated for the LX speed (see 3.13.9.3.5.11&12 for the calculation of this location).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.69

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.3.2, PDF p.70

5.16.3.2 As soon as the estimated or the max safe front end (depending whether the most restrictive SBI supervision limit at LX speed is the SBI1 or the SBI2, see 3.13.9.3.5.11) reaches the location of the Permitted speed supervision limit calculated for the LX speed, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall no longer supervise the LX start location as both the EOA and SvL (i.e. the EOA/LOA and the SvL (if any) derived from the MA shall be again supervised) and shall immediately include the LX speed restriction in the MRSP, starting from the train front end (estimated or max safe), which has reached the concerned Permitted speed supervision limit location. braking curve in FS/LS/OS mode Permitted speed supervision limit at LX speed speed LX Speed train speed train front end location Beginning of the LX area LX speed is supervised Figure 11: Approaching a non protected LX with stopping not required

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.16.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.16.3.3, PDF p.70

5.16.3.3 Note: A braking curve to zero, instead of a braking curve to the LX speed at the LX start location, will ensure that the train is able to stop before the start location of the level crossing, in case this latter is not free for the train to pass. Close to the level crossing it is then the responsibility of the driver to proceed or not with LX speed as a maximum.

5.17 Changing Train Data from sources different from the driver

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.17.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.17.1.1, PDF p.70

5.17.1.1 When valid Train Data is stored on-board, input information acquired from ERTMS/ETCS external sources different from the driver may affect some of the Train Data, depending on the type of train (e.g. tilting input information from tilting external device may affect the train category and the loading gauge).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.70

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.17.1.2, PDF p.71

5.17.1.2 The procedure here below describes the necessary steps performed by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment from the detection of an input information change on an external interface, to the effective encountering of the Train Data change by the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.17.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.17.1.3, PDF p.71

5.17.1.3 This procedure is not applicable for trains running in RV mode: on leaving RV mode, the Train Data will always be invalidated or deleted.

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.17.2, PDF p.71

5.17.2 Table of requirements for “Changing Train Data from sources different from the driver” procedure

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.17.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.17.2.1, PDF p.71

5.17.2.1 The ID numbers in the table are used for the representation of the procedure in form of a flow chart in section 5.17.3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.17.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.17.2.2, PDF p.71

5.17.2.2 Procedure ID # Requirements S0 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is in one of the following modes: FS, LS, OS, SR, SB, SN, UN, TR, PT and valid Train Data is stored on-board. If a change of input information, which affects Train Data, is detected on an ERTMS/ETCS on-board external interface (E0), the process shall go to D0 D0 According to the specific train implementation, Train Data which is/are affected by the change of input information from the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment external interface may require validation:  If the affected data requires driver validation, the process shall go to D2  If the affected data does not require driver validation, the process shall go to D1 D1 Depending on the type of Train Data which is/are affected by the change of input information from the ERTMS/ETCS on-board external interface, the following shall apply:  If the impacted Train Data regards either train category, or axle load category, or traction system(s) accepted by the engine, or loading gauge, the process shall go to D3  If the impacted Train Data regards any other type of Train Data, the process shall go to A1 D3 Depending on the mode of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment, the following shall apply:  If mode is FS, LS, or OS, the process shall go to D7  If mode is SB or PT, the process shall go to A1  If mode is UN, SN, SR, or TR the process shall go to D5

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.71

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP ID # Requirements D5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall check whether MA and track description, received from RBC, are stored on-board, in case a level 2/3 transition or a RBC transition for a further location has been ordered:  If MA and track description are stored, the process shall go to D7  If MA and track description are not both stored, the process shall go to A1 D7 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall check whether the train is at standstill:  If at standstill, the process shall go to A1  If not at standstill, the process shall go to S2 A1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall inform the driver that Train Data has been changed and the process shall go to A7 S2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall command the service brake, inform the driver about the reason of this brake command and waits for the train to be at standstill; when the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment detects that the train is at standstill (E2), the process shall go to S3 S3 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall request the driver to acknowledge the brake command; when the driver acknowledges (E3), the process shall go to A5 A5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall release the brake command and the process shall go to A7 D2 Depending on the mode of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment, the following shall apply:  If mode is FS, LS, OS, SR, SB, SN or UN the process shall go to D9  If mode is TR or PT, the process shall go to S1 S1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall wait for the end of the Train Trip procedure (see section 5.11). When the Train Trip procedure is exited (E1) (i.e. there is a mode transition to another mode than TR, PT), the process shall go to D4 D4 Depending on the mode of the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment, the following shall apply:  If mode is FS, LS, OS, SR, SN or UN the process shall go to S6  If mode is SH, the Train Data are invalidated and the process shall END D9 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall check whether the train is at standstill:  If at standstill, the process shall go to S6  If not at standstill, the process shall go to S4 S4 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall command the service brake, inform the driver about the reason of this brake command and wait for the train to be at standstill; when the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment detects that the train is at standstill (E4), the process shall go to S5

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.72

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP ID # Requirements S5 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall request the driver to acknowledge the brake command; when the driver acknowledges (E5), the process shall go to A6 A6 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall release the brake command and the process shall go to S6 S6 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall request the driver to re-enter or re- validate the Train Data. Once Train Data is validated (E6), the process shall go to A7 A7 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall consider the Train Data as being changed and shall apply, when relevant, the requirements regarding change of Train Data (refer to clauses 3.18.3.4, 3.18.3.7 and 3.18.3.8). The process shall END.

5.18.4 Passing a non stopping area

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.4.1, PDF p.78

5.18.4.1 This procedure is dealing with the announcement and indication to the driver of an area where stopping is not permitted.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.4.2, PDF p.78

5.18.4.2 As long as there are non stopping areas stored on-board, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall continuously check the current speed and position of the train whether a full service brake command would stop the train within any of the stored non stopping areas. This shall be achieved taking into account for each non stopping area, two virtual SBI supervision limits (SBI and SBI ), calculated at the estimated speed D G from two SBD curves of which the feet are the start location of the non stopping area (point D) and a location (point G) at train length distance in advance of the end location of the non stopping area: a) If the max safe front end is in rear of the first SBI supervision limit (SBI ) no D information related to this non stopping area shall be displayed b) If the max safe front end is in advance of the first SBI supervision limit (SBI ) and D the min safe front end in rear of the second SBI supervision limit (SBI ), the non G stopping area related information shall be displayed to the driver according to the following clauses 5.18.4.3, 5.18.4.4. c) If the min safe front end is in advance of the second SBI supervision limit (SBI ), no G information related to this non stopping area shall be displayed.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.4.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.4.3, PDF p.78

5.18.4.3 When the max safe front end is in rear of the start location (point D) of the non stopping area, the “Non stopping area announcement” shall be displayed to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.4.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.4.4, PDF p.78

5.18.4.4 When the max safe front end is in advance of the start location (point D) of the non stopping area:  “Non stopping area announcement”, if any, shall no longer be displayed

5.18.8 Advising a tunnel stopping area

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.8.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.8.1, PDF p.82

5.18.8.1 This procedure is dealing with the indication to the driver of an area under a tunnel where stopping is permitted, and suitable escaping paths are provided.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.8.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.8.1.1, PDF p.82

5.18.8.1.1 Note: the tunnel stopping areas are designed in such a way that the passengers can step out, use a walkway along the track and reach the safe area, taking into account the longest admissible train in the tunnel stopped with its front end within the tunnel stopping area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.8.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.8.2, PDF p.82

5.18.8.2 On driver request, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall enable/disable the display of the tunnel stopping area related information (initial state: disabled).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.82

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.8.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.8.3, PDF p.83

5.18.8.3 As long as the display of the tunnel stopping areas is enabled (point C) and there are tunnel stopping areas stored on-board, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall continuously check the current speed and position of the train to determine whether the driver can stop the train with the full service brake before reaching the end of the closest tunnel stopping area. This shall be achieved taking into account a virtual Permitted supervision limit (with no contribution of the GUI curve, if any), calculated at the estimated speed from an SBD curve of which the foot is the end location of the tunnel stopping area: a) If the train front end is in rear of the Permitted supervision limit, the tunnel stopping area related information shall be displayed to the driver. b) If the train front end is in advance of the Permitted supervision limit, no information related to this tunnel stopping area shall be displayed and the next tunnel stopping area stored on-board, if any, shall be checked.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.8.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.8.4, PDF p.83

5.18.8.4 Before the train reaches the start location (point D) of the tunnel stopping area, the “tunnel stopping area announcement” shall be displayed to the driver. This shall include the indication of the remaining distance to the start location of the tunnel stopping area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.18.8.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.18.8.5, PDF p.83

5.18.8.5 When the train front end reaches the start location (point D) of the tunnel stopping area:  “Tunnel stopping area announcement” shall no longer be displayed  “Tunnel stopping area” information shall be displayed to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.1.1, PDF p.86

5.19.1.1 The order to switch to Limited Supervision mode shall be given by means of a mode profile.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.1.2, PDF p.86

5.19.1.2 An acknowledgement for running in Limited Supervision mode shall be requested from the driver. The conditions of the acknowledgement are specified below.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2, PDF p.86

5.19.2 Limited Supervision is requested for current location (from modes different from Stand By and Post Trip)

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2.1, PDF p.86

5.19.2.1 In a level 1 area, the beginning of the Limited Supervision area can be the balise (group) that gives the Mode Profile. When the train passes the balise group and receives this information, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately switch to Limited Supervision mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2.2, PDF p.86

5.19.2.2 In a level 2 or 3 area, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment can receive a mode profile giving a Limited Supervision area which the train has already entered with its max safe front end. In this case, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall immediately switch to Limited Supervision mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2.3, PDF p.86

5.19.2.3 The driver must acknowledge the Limited Supervision mode. A request of acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2.4, PDF p.86

5.19.2.4 If the driver has not acknowledged after the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A.3.1), the service brake command shall be triggered. The brake command is released when the driver acknowledges, except if brakes are also applied for another reason(s).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2.5, PDF p.86

5.19.2.5 Note: Once in Limited Supervision mode, the speed supervision is such that the train speed cannot exceed the LS mode speed limit. If, when entering the Limited Supervision mode, the train speed was higher than the LS mode speed limit (because a higher speed was allowed in Full Supervision mode, On Sight mode or in Staff Responsible mode) then an emergency brake command could be immediately triggered, independently of the acknowledgement of the driver, but because of the LS supervision (see Figure 22).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.86

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP Transition to LS mode triggers EB command speed permitted speed (even if driver acknowledges in previous mode within 5s) Brake command revoked (conditions see SRS chapter 3, Dynamic Speed Monitoring) train speed permitted speed in LS mode Location of: LS request for location current location Figure 22: Train enters LS area with too high speed

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2.6, PDF p.87

5.19.2.6 Note: This sharp brake reaction can be avoided in Full Supervision or On Sight mode by giving with the previous MA an EOA (or a LOA = LS mode speed limit) at the location of transition to Limited Supervision mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.2.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.2.7, PDF p.87

5.19.2.7 If the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is already in LS mode when receiving the LS mode profile, no further acknowledgement shall be requested from the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3, PDF p.87

5.19.3 Limited Supervision is requested for a further location

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.1, PDF p.87

5.19.3.1 The beginning of the Limited Supervision area can be a location that the train has not reached yet. This occurs when: a) In a level 1 area, a balise group gives a Mode Profile with an Limited Supervision area that is located at a further location. b) In a level 2 or 3 area, the RBC gives a Mode Profile with an Limited Supervision area that is located at a further location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.2, PDF p.87

5.19.3.2 A request for acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver when the following conditions are fulfilled: a) The distance between the estimated front end of the train and the beginning of Limited Supervision area is shorter than a value, contained in the mode profile. b) The speed is lower than the Limited Supervision mode speed limit (national value, or value given in the mode profile). c) The current mode is not Limited Supervision

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.3, PDF p.87

5.19.3.3 Note: The first 2 conditions define the “rectangle of acknowledgement”.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.4, PDF p.87

5.19.3.4 Once the acknowledgement request is displayed, it shall not be taken back if the train leaves the “rectangle of acknowledgement” (for example: because the train accelerates).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.87

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.5, PDF p.88

5.19.3.5 Until the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment has switched to LS mode, the beginning of the Limited Supervision area shall be temporarily considered as the EOA (instead of the EOA/LOA derived from the MA) and the SvL (with no release speed) shall be determined according to the mode profile either: a) as the SvL derived from the MA. In case the MA defines an LOA, the SvL shall be derived as if no LOA had been given. OR b) as the beginning of the Limited Supervision area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.6, PDF p.88

5.19.3.6 When the driver acknowledges the Limited Supervision mode, the ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment shall immediately switch to the Limited Supervision mode. braking curve e.g. in FS mode acknowledge request is speed displayed to the driver driver acknowledges train speed Permitted Speed In LS mode location Beginning of the Acknowledgement Limited Supervision area Area Transition to Limited Supervision mode Figure 23: Transition to LS mode after driver acknowledgement

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.7, PDF p.88

5.19.3.7 If the max safe front end of the train reaches the beginning of the Limited Supervision area according the mode profile and the driver has not yet acknowledged, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall switch immediately to LS mode and a request for acknowledgement shall be displayed to the driver (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.3.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.3.8, PDF p.88

5.19.3.8 If, in this case, the driver does not acknowledge within the driver acknowledgement time (refer to Appendix A.3.1) after the change to LS mode, the service brake command shall be triggered. The command shall be released as soon as the driver acknowledges (unless the command was triggered also for other reasons).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.88

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.4, PDF p.89

5.19.4 Limited Supervision from Unfitted or SN mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.4.1, PDF p.89

5.19.4.1 The mode profile with regards to an LS area is only evaluated in levels 1,2,3, although the mode profile may have been received in level 0 (Unfitted mode) or NTC (SN mode). A transition to Limited Supervision mode can therefore earliest occur at a transition of level: from level 0 or NTC to level 1 or 2 or 3.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.4.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.4.2, PDF p.89

5.19.4.2 Requirements about the acknowledgement in section 5.19.2 shall apply.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.5, PDF p.89

5.19.5 Limited Supervision from Stand By or Post Trip mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.5.1, PDF p.89

5.19.5.1 When performing a SoM or a Train Trip procedure and when the current level is 2 or 3, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment can receive a mode profile giving an Limited Supervision area which the train has already entered with its max safe front end. In this case, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall first require an acknowledgement from the driver.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.5.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.5.2, PDF p.89

5.19.5.2 When the driver acknowledges, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall perform the transition to Limited Supervision mode.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6, PDF p.89

5.19.6 Exit of Limited Supervision mode

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6.1.1, PDF p.89

5.19.6.1.1 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall exit the Limited Supervision mode when the min safe front end of the train passes the end of the Limited supervision area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6.2, PDF p.89

5.19.6.2 First case: The Limited supervision area ends at the EOA/LOA of the current MA

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6.2.1, PDF p.89

5.19.6.2.1 This occurs when the end of the Limited Supervision area that is given by the Mode Profile has the same location as the EOA/LOA of the related MA.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6.2.2, PDF p.89

5.19.6.2.2 In this case, the train must receive a new Movement Authority to be able to exit the Limited Supervision area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6.3, PDF p.89

5.19.6.3 Second case: The Limited Supervision area ends before the EOA/LOA of the current MA

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6.3.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6.3.1, PDF p.89

5.19.6.3.1 In this case, the current Movement Authority already allows the train to exit the Limited Supervision area.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.19.6.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.19.6.3.2, PDF p.89

5.19.6.3.2 When exiting the Limited Supervision area, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment switches either to Full Supervision, On Sight or to Shunting mode (refer to SRS chapter 4, transitions between modes).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.89

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20, PDF p.91

5.20 Generation of Track Conditions related information to an ERTMS/ETCS external function

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.1.1, PDF p.91

5.20.1.1 This set of procedures specifies the information generated by the ERTMS/ETCS on- board equipment to an ERTMS/ETCS external function in relation to the following track-conditions: a) powerless section with pantograph to be lowered, b) powerless section with main power switch to be switched off, c) passing an “air tightness” area, d) inhibition of a defined type of brake, e) change of traction system, f) change of allowed current consumption, g) station platform.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.1.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.1.2, PDF p.91

5.20.1.2 In the following sections, the remaining distance from the concerned train end to the concerned track condition location shall be counted positive when the train end is in rear of the location and shall be counted negative when the train end is in advance of the location.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2, PDF p.91

5.20.2 Passing a powerless section with pantograph to be lowered

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.1, PDF p.91

5.20.2.1 This procedure is dealing with the generation of the information related to a powerless section with the pantograph to be lowered.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.2

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.2, PDF p.91

5.20.2.2 The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall start the generation of the information to the ERTMS/ETCS external function when the max safe front end of the train reaches the point C in rear of the start location of the powerless section (see 5.18.2.2.1 for the definition of point C).

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.3

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.3, PDF p.91

5.20.2.3 When the min safe rear end of the train is in rear of the start location (point D) of the powerless section, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall provide the following information to the ERTMS/ETCS external function:  the remaining distance from the max safe front end of the train to the start location (point D) of the powerless section  the remaining distance from the min safe front end of the train to the end location (point E) of the powerless section

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.4

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.4, PDF p.91

5.20.2.4 When the min safe rear end of the train reaches the start location (point D) of the powerless section, the remaining distance from the max safe front end of the train to point D shall no longer be generated. The remaining distance from the min safe front

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 3.6.0

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 3.6.0, PDF p.91

3.6.0 Chapter 5 13/05/2016 Procedures ERA * UNISIG * EEIG ERTMS USERS GROUP end of the train to the end location (point E) of the powerless section shall continue to be generated.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.5

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.5, PDF p.92

5.20.2.5 When the min safe rear end of the train reaches the end location (point E) of the powerless section, the remaining distance from the min safe front end of the train to point E shall no longer be generated.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.6

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.6, PDF p.92

5.20.2.6 Note: The remaining distance from the train max safe front end to point D and the remaining distance from the train min safe front end to point E are generated until the min safe rear end passes respectively the point D and the point E to allow the ERTMS/ETCS external function to manage each pantograph individually assuming that this function knows the distance between each pantograph and the train front end. running direction A Generate the remaining distance to point D Generate the remaining and the remaining distance to point E distance to point E C D E LRBG Powerless section Distance to start of powerless section Powerless section length Figure 25: Generation of the information to an ERTMS/ETCS external function for a supervision of powerless section with pantograph to be lowered

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.7

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.7, PDF p.92

5.20.2.7 Note: When resuming the initial state (see 3.7.3.2) or any other reason (e.g. see Appendix A.3.4) leads to the shortening of a powerless section with pantograph to be lowered, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment considers the new end location (point E) of the powerless section for the calculation of the remaining distance from the min safe front end of the train to the point E.

SUBSET-026 v3.6.0 — clause 5.20.2.8

Citation: SUBSET-026 v3.6.0, clause 5.20.2.8, PDF p.92

5.20.2.8 If resuming the initial state (see 3.7.3.2) or any other reason (e.g. see Appendix A.3.4) leads to the deletion of the powerless section, the ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment shall stop providing information related to this powerless section to the ERTMS/ETCS external function.

4g.1........................................................................................................................ 128 Version 3.1.0 Level Transitions STM to ETCS TEST CASE DIAGRAMS Overview For testing of the Functional Identity “Level Transition STM to ETCS” 7 Test Case Diagrams and 12 Test Cases have been defined. One additional diagram has been defined and two additional preliminary test cases can be executed for setting of the relevant starting conditions (level transition announcement, request of DMI objects from STM to ETCS DMI function, etc.). Requirements coverage is out of the scope of these preliminary test cases. Exception: for the test group 4g (Double Level Transition during NTP transition), the preliminary conditions can be set at the end of the sequence 5b.0.4 (level border) (defined in Subset 074-2-5 “Functional Identity 005 Level Transitions STM to STM”). Announcement STM DMI 5b – Between area and STM object announcement DMI object Pre-scenario activation and transition activation 4a 4b 4c 4d 4e 4g Level Leveltransition Level transition Level transition Level transition Double Level transition in SN in NL mode in SL mode during a NTP with driver transition mode manual during NTP selection 4f Emergency Brake Release In the test case descriptions all “optional” actions, conditions or input/outputs related to specific STM and ETCS configurations are remarked allowing a correct test results analysis. SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.3.2

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.3.2, PDF p.7

13.4.3.2 The STM shall request the display of an Indicator by means of the following definition: a) its Indicator Identifier, b) an optional Icon Identifier, c) an optional caption text, d) a Position Identifier, e) a display attribute.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.2.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.2.1, PDF p.7

13.4.2.1 The DMI Function shall display a text message when requested by the STM. The text message request shall consist of a Text Identifier, a string of text to be shown to the driver, a display attribute and a possible request for driver acknowledgement.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.4.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.4.1, PDF p.7

13.4.4.1 Buttons are a pure functional extension of Indicators. All requirements of chapter 13.4.3 shall apply to Buttons, by replacing “Indicators” with “Button”.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.5.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 13.4.5.1, PDF p.7

13.4.5.1 STM shall request a sound by means of the following definition: a) an optional Sound Identifier, b) only in case of a unified DMI and a Sound to be generated, a sequence of segments defined by a duration and an associated frequency, c) an indication if the Sound has to be repeated continuously or not or to be stopped.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 13.4.6.4

9.2.1.3 Note: As long as an STM in DA state is in a National Trip Procedure in SN Mode, the STM sends cyclically the “National Trip Procedure” information to the STM Control Function in order to fulfil the timeout requirements defined in 10.3.2.4 (transition E16 and F16). If the mode changes to TR, the STM is expected to enter CS state even if its National Trip Procedure is not finished, as the Trip procedure is handed over by ERTMS/ETCS on-board (otherwise, the STM would be ordered to FA state through transition Q16 once the TR mode is exited).

10.3.2.4 - A4b (ERTMS/ETCS on-board performs a level transition ordered by the trackside from Level NTC X to NTC Y) AND (STM X is different from the STM Y associated to Level NTC Y)

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 10.3.2.7

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 10.3.2.7, PDF p.14

10.3.2.7 When the state transition order is going to CS state, the STM Control Function shall send an “unconditional order CS state” for the transitions A4a, B4a, C4a, E4a, G4a, H4a, I4a, J4a, K4a and L4a, and a “conditional order CS state” for the transitions A4b and B4b.

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 10.3.3.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 10.3.3.3, PDF p.14

10.3.3.3 The STM Control Function shall command the emergency brake from the moment a “conditional CS state transition order” has been sent to a STM and this STM is in National Trip Procedure, up to the moment this STM reports CS state, or is considered as failed and the train reaches standstill

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.2.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.2.1.3, PDF p.14

9.2.1.3 Note: As long as an STM in DA state is in a National Trip Procedure in SN mode, the STM sends cyclically the “National Trip Procedure” information to the STM Control Function in order to fulfil the timeout requirements defined in 10.3.2.4 (transitions E16 and F16). If the mode changes to TR, the STM is expected to enter CS state even if its National Trip Procedure is not finished, as the Trip procedure is handed over by ERTMS/ETCS on-board (otherwise, the STM would be ordered to FA state through transition Q16 once the TR mode is exited).” 0 At standstill the driver selects Level 0 SRS 4.6.3 Transitions Conditions Table [38] (The ERTMS/ETCS on-board equipment is interfaced to the National System through an STM) AND (The ERTMS/ETCS level switches to 0,1,2 or 3) AND (a National Trip Procedure is active)

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 10.5.1.1

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 10.5.1.1, PDF p.14

10.5.1.1 The STM Control Function shall send the ETCS status data consisting of the current ETCS mode and level (defined in [1]): a) To all connected STMs whenever the ETCS mode or level changes. b) To any STM when the connection to the STM Control Function is established 0 STM(X) reports again NTP and the driver acknowledges TR

SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0 — clause 9.2.1.3

Citation: SUBSET-074-2 v3.1.0, clause 9.2.1.3, PDF p.14

9.2.1.3 Note: As long as an STM in DA state is in a National Trip Procedure in SN mode, the STM sends cyclically the “National Trip Procedure” information to the STM Control Function in order to fulfil the timeout requirements defined in 10.3.2.4 (transitions E16 and F16). If the mode changes to TR, the STM is expected to enter CS state even if its National Trip Procedure is not finished, as the Trip procedure is handed over by ERTMS/ETCS on-board (otherwise, the STM would be ordered to FA state through transition Q16 once the TR mode is exited).”

ERTMS/ETCS on-board Subset 035: 10.3.2.2 (DACS and DAFA), 10.3.2.4 (B4a and C16), 10.3.2.6, 10.3.2.7(B4a), 10.3.3.1, 10.5.1.1(a), 10.14.1.1, requirements tested 13.2.1.2 STM Requirements Tested - Packets transmitted via - from STM to ETCS: - FFFIS STM - from ETCS to STM: STM-5, STM-14 ERTMS/ETCS on-board - No DMI configuration for active STM: Unified DMI shall be used for the test configuration - the number of STMs configured on (and connected to) the ETCS is not relevant: only one STM can be in DA state Comments and constraints - Preliminary Test Case (4a, 4b, 4d) to be executed as precondition - Only level 1 transition is tested because there is no difference with transitions to level 0, 2 or 3 at FFFIS STM interface level; - The test case applies only to ERTMS/ETCS on-board because from the STM point of view this is a degraded situation. Function one. Scope of the test case is to verify that: - when ERTMS/ETCS on-board in SN mode executes a level transition from NTC (during an active National Trip Procedure) to ETCS level 1, STM Control Function orders the STM in CS state and, - STM Control Function deletes all DMI objects after CS order and, - if STM reports CS state in due time, it can close the active connections except the STM Control Function one. ERTMS/ETCS on-board Subset 035: 8.7.1.2, 10.3.2.2 (DACS), 10.3.2.4 (B4a), 10.3.2.6, 10.3.2.7(B4a), 10.5.1.1(a), 10.13.1.1, 13.2.1.2, requirements tested Subset 026: 4.6.3 [38] STM Requirements Tested Subset 035: 8.7.1.2, 9.2.1.1 (DACS), 9.2.1.2 (4a), 9.3.1.4(c) Packets transmitted via - from STM to ETCS: STM-18, STM-15 FFFIS STM - from ETCS to STM: STM-5, STM-14, ERTMS/ETCS on-board - No DMI configuration for active STM: Unified DMI shall be used for the test configuration - the number of STMs configured on (and connected to) the ETCS is not relevant: only one STM can be in DA state Comments and constraints - Preliminary Test Case (4a, 4b, 4d) to be executed as precondition - Only level 1 transition is tested because there is no difference with transitions to level 0, 2 or 3 at FFFIS STM interface level; - In STM Test case NTP shall be triggered according to the specific constraints and procedures of STM under test. - ETCS Test Case designed for testing ETCS when STM ordered in CS closes all the connections except STM Control Function; - STM test case is designed for both STMs that, when ordered in CS, close all the connections except STM Control Functions or keep all connections active; - STM test case is designed only for STMs that use NTP procedures. when ERTMS/ETCS on-board in SN mode executes a level transition from NTC to ETCS level 0 cause of driver selection on DMI, STM Control Function orders the STM in CS state and, - STM Control Function deletes all DMI objects after CS order and, - if STM reports CS state in due time, it can close active connections except STM Control Function one. ERTMS/ETCS on-board Subset 035: 8.7.1.2, 10.3.2.2 (DACS), 10.3.2.4 (K4a), 10.3.2.6, 10.3.2.7(K4a), 10.5.1.1(a), 13.2.1.2 requirements tested STM Requirements Tested Subset 035: 8.7.1.2, 9.2.1.1 (DACS), 9.2.1.2 (4a), 9.3.1.4(c) Packets transmitted via - from STM to ETCS: STM-15, FFFIS STM - from ETCS to STM: STM-5, STM-14 ERTMS/ETCS on-board - No DMI configuration for active STM: Unified DMI shall be used for the test configuration - the number of STMs configured on (and connected to) the ETCS is not relevant: only one STM can be in DA state Comments and constraints - Preliminary Test Case (4e) to be executed as precondition - Only level 0 transition is tested because there is no difference with transitions to level 1, 2 or 3 at FFFIS STM interface level; - ETCS Test Case designed for testing ETCS when STM ordered in CS closes all the connections except STM Control Function; - STM test case is designed for both STMs that, when ordered in CS, close all the connections except STM Control Functions or keep all connections active. Scope of the test case is to verify that: - After a level transition of the STM (X) from Level NTC (X) to Level NTC (Y), when the ERTMS/ETCS on-board in SN mode executes a transition from Level NTC (Y) to ETCS Level 0 (or Level 1, 2 or 3), if the STM(X) reports again the National Trip Procedure, the STM Control Function orders the STM(X) in FA state.
